title.en: Volume 142 Biographies 92: Li Baochen, Wang Wujun, Wang Tingcou

sentences.zh: 薛播薛播，河中寶鼎人，中書舍人文思曾孫也。

translations.literal: Xue Bo—Xue Bo was a native of Baoding in Hezhong, a great-grandson of the Attendant Gentleman Wen Si.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Bo was from Baoding in Hezhong. He was the great-grandson of Wen Si, who had served as Attendant Gentleman at the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 父元暉，什邡令，以播贈工部郎中。

translations.literal: His father Yuan Hui was magistrate of Shifang; because of Bo he was posthumously enfeoffed as Director in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yuan Hui had been magistrate of Shifang; on Bo's account Yuan Hui was posthumously granted the title Director in the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 播，天寶中舉進士，補校書郎，累授萬年縣丞、武功令、殿中侍御史、刑部員外郎、萬年令。

translations.literal: Bo, in the Tianbao era passed the jinshi examination, was appointed Collator, and was repeatedly appointed Assistant Magistrate of Wannian, Magistrate of Wugong, Attendant Censor within the Palace, Vice Director in the Ministry of Justice, and Magistrate of Wannian.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianbao reign Bo passed the jinshi examination and entered service as a Collator. He rose through a series of posts: Assistant Magistrate of Wannian, Magistrate of Wugong, Palace Attendant Censor, Vice Director in the Ministry of Justice, and again Magistrate of Wannian.

sentences.zh: 播溫敏，善與人交，李棲筠、常袞、崔祐甫皆引擢之。

translations.literal: Bo was gentle and quick-witted, skilled at forming friendships; Li Qiyun, Chang Gun, and Cui Youfu all drew him up and promoted him.
translations.idiomatic: Bo was affable and quick-witted and excelled at cultivating relationships. Li Qiyun, Chang Gun, and Cui Youfu each took him up and advanced his career.

sentences.zh: 及祐甫輔政，用為中書舍人。

translations.literal: When Youfu came to assist in government, he was employed as Attendant Gentleman at the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Once Youfu assumed a leading role at court, Bo was appointed Attendant Gentleman at the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 出汝州刺史，以公事貶泉州刺史。

translations.literal: He went out as Prefect of Ruzhou; for an official matter he was demoted to Prefect of Quanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out to serve as Prefect of Ruzhou, then demoted to Prefect of Quanzhou on account of an official infraction.

sentences.zh: 尋除晉州刺史，河南尹，遷尚書左丞，轉禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: Soon he was removed to be Prefect of Jinzhou and Intendant of Henan, was transferred to Left Vice Director of the Secretariat, and turned to Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed Prefect of Jinzhou and Intendant of Henan, then promoted to Left Vice Director of the Secretariat and finally Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 遇疾，貞元三年卒，贈禮部尚書。

translations.literal: He encountered illness; in the third year of Zhenyuan he died, and was posthumously enfeoffed as Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He fell ill and died in the third year of the Zhenyuan era (787). He was posthumously granted the title Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 初，播伯父元曖終於隰城丞，其妻濟南林氏，丹陽太守洋之妹，有母儀令德，博涉《五經》，善屬文，所為篇章，時人多諷詠之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Bo's paternal uncle Yuan Ai died while serving as Assistant Magistrate of Xicheng. His wife, Lady Lin of Jinan—a younger sister of Yang, Prefect of Danyang—possessed the deportment of a mother and outstanding virtue. She was broadly versed in the Five Classics and skilled at literary composition; the pieces she wrote were widely chanted and sung in her day.
translations.idiomatic: Bo's uncle Yuan Ai had died in office as Assistant Magistrate of Xicheng, leaving a widow, Lady Lin of Jinan, younger sister of the Danyang prefect Yang. She was a woman of exemplary bearing and learning, well read in the Five Classics and accomplished as a writer; contemporaries often recited her compositions.

sentences.zh: 元曖卒後，其子彥輔、彥國、彥偉、彥雲及播兄據、摠並早孤幼，悉為林氏所訓導，以至成立，咸致文學之名。

translations.literal: After Yuan Ai died, his sons Yanfu, Yanguo, Yanwei, and Yanyun, together with Bo's elder brothers Ju and Zong, were all orphaned young; all were instructed and guided by Lady Lin until they came of age, and all attained renown in letters.
translations.idiomatic: After Yuan Ai's death his sons Yanfu, Yanguo, Yanwei, and Yanyun, along with Bo's elder brothers Ju and Zong, were left fatherless while still children. Lady Lin raised and tutored them all to maturity, and each won a reputation for literary accomplishment.

sentences.zh: 開元、天寶中二十年間，彥輔、據等七人並舉進士，連中科名，衣冠榮之。

translations.literal: Within the twenty years of the Kaiyuan and Tianbao eras, Yanfu, Ju, and the other seven all passed the jinshi examination in succession, winning consecutive examination honors, to the glory of the gentry.
translations.idiomatic: Over the twenty years spanning the Kaiyuan and Tianbao reigns, all seven—Yanfu, Ju, and the rest—passed the jinshi examination one after another, a run of successes that became the pride of their clan.

sentences.zh: 鮑防鮑防，襄州人。

translations.literal: Bao Fang—Bao Fang was a native of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Bao Fang was a native of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 幼孤貧，篤誌好學，善屬文。

translations.literal: Orphaned young and poor, he was steadfast in purpose and fond of learning, and skilled at literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned in childhood and raised in poverty, he pursued his studies with single-minded devotion and showed a gift for writing.

sentences.zh: 天寶末舉進士，為漸東觀察使薛兼訓從事，累至殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: At the end of Tianbao he passed the jinshi examination, served as aide to Xue Jianxun, Military Governor of Zhedong, and was repeatedly promoted to Attendant Censor within the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Near the close of the Tianbao era he passed the jinshi examination and joined the staff of Xue Jianxun, governor of Zhedong, rising eventually to Palace Attendant Censor.

sentences.zh: 入為職方員外郎，改太原少尹，正拜節度使。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as Vice Director in the Bureau of Appointments, was changed to Vice Intendant of Taiyuan, and was formally appointed Military Governor.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to the capital as Vice Director in the Bureau of Appointments, then appointed Vice Intendant of Taiyuan and finally invested as full Military Governor.

sentences.zh: 入為御史大夫，歷福建、江西觀察使，徵拜左散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He entered as Censor-in-Chief, served successively as Military Governor of Fujian and Jiangxi, and was summoned and appointed Left Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to court as Censor-in-Chief, served as governor of Fujian and then Jiangxi, and was summoned back to receive appointment as Left Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 扈從奉天，除禮部侍郎，尋遷工部尚書致仕。

translations.literal: He followed in attendance at Fengtian, was appointed Vice Minister of Rites, and soon was transferred to Minister of Works and retired.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied the emperor to Fengtian, was made Vice Minister of Rites, and soon after promoted to Minister of Works before retiring from office.

sentences.zh: 防歷洪、福、京兆，皆有政聲，唯總戎非所宜，而謬執兵柄。

translations.literal: Fang served in Hong, Fu, and Jingzhao, and in all had a reputation for good government; only overall command of troops was not suitable for him, yet he wrongly grasped the military authority.
translations.idiomatic: In his stints governing Hong, Fu, and the capital region he earned a reputation for capable administration, but command of armies was not his strength—yet he insisted on holding military authority.

sentences.zh: 以太原革車胡騎雄雜，而回鶻深入寇，防出拒戰，為虜所敗。

translations.literal: Because Taiyuan had many fierce and mixed Hu cavalry among its leather-armored chariots, and the Uyghurs raided deep in invasion, Fang went out to resist and fight, and was defeated by the barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Taiyuan's forces included large numbers of fierce nomadic cavalry. When the Uyghurs launched a deep raid, Fang marched out to meet them and was routed.

sentences.zh: 為禮部侍郎時，嘗遇知雜侍御史竇參於通衢，導騎不時引避，仆人為參所鞭；

translations.literal: When he was Vice Minister of Rites, he once encountered the Attendant Censor in charge of miscellaneous matters, Dou Can, on a main thoroughfare; the outriders did not yield in time, and a servant was flogged by Can.
translations.idiomatic: While serving as Vice Minister of Rites he once met the supervising censor Dou Can on a public road. His escort failed to clear the way promptly, and Can had one of Fang's servants whipped.

sentences.zh: 及參秉政，遽令致仕。

translations.literal: When Can took hold of government, he was abruptly ordered to retire.
translations.idiomatic: Once Dou Can seized power at court, Fang was abruptly forced into retirement.

sentences.zh: 防謂親友曰：「吾與蕭昕之子齒，而與昕同日懸車，非朽邁之致，以余忿見廢。

translations.literal: Fang said to relatives and friends: "I am of an age with Xiao Xin's son, yet I retire from office on the same day as Xin—it is not due to decrepitude and advanced years, but because I was dismissed through Can's resentment."
translations.idiomatic: Fang told friends and kin, "I am the same age as Xiao Xin's son, yet I am retiring on the very day Xin does—not because I am worn out with age, but because Can's grudge has undone me."

sentences.zh: 」防文學舊人，歷職中外，不因罪戾，而為俗吏所擯，竟以憤終。

translations.literal: Fang was an old man of letters, who served in posts inside and outside the capital, not because of crime or offense, yet was ostracized by vulgar clerks, and in the end died from indignation.
translations.idiomatic: A veteran man of letters who had served at court and in the provinces, Fang was driven out not for any crime but by a coarse official's spite, and he died embittered.

sentences.zh: 眾頗憫防而咎參，故參之敗不旋踵，非不幸也。

translations.literal: The multitude greatly pitied Fang and blamed Can; therefore Can's downfall came without turning the heel—this was not misfortune.
translations.idiomatic: Public sympathy lay with Fang and blame with Can, so when Can's fall followed almost at once, few regarded it as undeserved.

sentences.zh: 李自良李自良，兗州泗水人。

translations.literal: Li Ziliang—Li Ziliang was a native of Sishui in Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ziliang was a native of Sishui in Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 初，祿山之亂，自良從兗鄆節度使能元皓，以戰功累授右衛率。

translations.literal: At first, during the rebellion of Lushan, Ziliang followed Neng Yuanhao, Military Governor of Yan-He, and through battle achievements was repeatedly appointed Right Commander of the Guard.
translations.idiomatic: When the An Lushan rebellion broke out, Ziliang served under Neng Yuanhao, military governor of Yan and He, and won repeated promotion for his battlefield record, eventually rising to Right Commander of the Guard.

sentences.zh: 後從袁傪討袁晁陳莊賊，積功至試殿中監，隸浙江東道節度使薛兼訓。

translations.literal: Later he followed Yuan Zai in campaigning against the bandits Yuan Chao and Chen Zhuang, accumulated merit to Acting Director within the Palace, and was attached to Xue Jianxun, Military Governor of Zhedong.
translations.idiomatic: He later campaigned under Yuan Zai against the rebels Yuan Chao and Chen Zhuang, accumulating enough merit to be named Acting Director within the Palace, and was assigned to the staff of Xue Jianxun, governor of Zhedong.

sentences.zh: 兼訓移鎮太原，自良從行，授河東軍節度押衙。

translations.literal: Jianxun transferred his command to Taiyuan; Ziliang followed on the march and was appointed Military Aide of the Hedong Army under the Military Governor.
translations.idiomatic: When Jianxun transferred his headquarters to Taiyuan, Ziliang went with him and was appointed chief military aide of the Hedong command.

sentences.zh: 兼訓卒，鮑防代，又事防為牙將。

translations.literal: Jianxun died; Bao Fang replaced him, and Ziliang again served Fang as a guard officer.
translations.idiomatic: After Jianxun's death Bao Fang succeeded him, and Ziliang continued in service as one of Fang's guard officers.

sentences.zh: 會回鶻入寇，防令大將焦伯瑜、杜榮國將兵擊之。

translations.literal: When the Uyghurs invaded, Fang ordered the great generals Jiao Boyu and Du Rongguo to lead troops and strike them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Uyghurs raided, Fang ordered his generals Jiao Boyu and Du Rongguo to take the field against them.

sentences.zh: 自良謂防曰：「回鶻遠來求戰，未可與爭鋒。

translations.literal: Ziliang said to Fang: "The Uyghurs have come from afar seeking battle; one must not contend with them at the spearpoint."
translations.idiomatic: Ziliang told Fang, "The Uyghurs have marched a great distance eager to fight. We should not meet them head-on."

sentences.zh: 但於歸路築二壘，以兵守之，堅壁不動，虜求戰不得，師老自旋。

translations.literal: Only build two forts on their route of return, garrison them with troops, hold the walls firm without moving; the barbarians will seek battle and not obtain it, the army will grow weary and turn back of itself.
translations.idiomatic: Instead, erect two fortified posts along their line of retreat and man them. Hold fast without giving battle. Denied a fight, their troops will tire and withdraw on their own."

sentences.zh: 俟其返昪，即乘之，縱不甚捷，虜必狼狽矣。

translations.literal: Wait until they return in high spirits, then mount and strike them; even if not very victorious, the barbarians will surely be in distress.
translations.idiomatic: When they turn back in high spirits, strike at once. Even a modest success will leave them in disarray."

sentences.zh: 二壘阨其歸路，策之上也。

translations.literal: Two forts blocking their route of return—this is the superior stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: Blocking their retreat with two forts—that is the best plan."

sentences.zh: 」防不從，促伯瑜等逆戰，遇虜於百井。

translations.literal: Fang did not follow this, urged Boyu and the others to meet the enemy in battle, and encountered the barbarians at Baijing.
translations.idiomatic: Fang refused. He pressed Boyu and the others to give battle and met the enemy at Baijing.

sentences.zh: 伯瑜等大敗而還，由是稍知名。

translations.literal: Boyu and the others returned in great defeat; from this Ziliang became slightly known by name.
translations.idiomatic: Boyu and his command were routed. Ziliang's counsel, ignored, nonetheless brought him a measure of notice.

sentences.zh: 馬燧代防為帥，署奏自良代州刺史、兼御史大夫，仍為軍候。

translations.literal: Ma Sui replaced Fang as commander; he memorialized and appointed Ziliang Prefect of Daizhou and concurrently Censor-in-Chief, and still made him army adjutant.
translations.idiomatic: When Ma Sui replaced Fang as commander, he had Ziliang appointed Prefect of Daizhou and concurrent Censor-in-Chief while retaining him as army adjutant.

sentences.zh: 自良勤恪有謀，燧深委信之。

translations.literal: Ziliang was diligent, respectful, and possessed of stratagems; Sui deeply entrusted and trusted him.
translations.idiomatic: Diligent, resourceful, and utterly dependable, Ziliang won Ma Sui's deepest trust.

sentences.zh: 建中年，田悅叛，燧與抱真東討；

translations.literal: In the Jianzhong years Tian Yue rebelled; Sui together with Bao Zhen campaigned east to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jianzhong era, when Tian Yue rebelled, Ma Sui marched east with Bao Zhen to suppress him.

sentences.zh: 自良常為河東大將，摧鋒陷陣，破田悅。

translations.literal: Ziliang often served as the great general of Hedong, shattered the vanguard and stormed the battle lines, and defeated Tian Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Ziliang regularly led the Hedong vanguard, breaking enemy lines and helping bring Tian Yue to defeat.

sentences.zh: 及討李懷光於河中，自良專河東軍都將，前後戰績居多。

translations.literal: When campaigning against Li Huai'guang at Hezhong, Ziliang alone was Chief General of the Hedong Army; before and after, battle achievements were mostly his.
translations.idiomatic: In the campaign against Li Huai'guang at Hezhong he served as chief commander of the Hedong forces and accounted for the lion's share of their victories.

sentences.zh: 燧之立功名，由自良協輔之力也。

translations.literal: Sui's establishment of fame and merit was through the power of Ziliang's cooperative assistance.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Sui's reputation and achievements owed much to Ziliang's support on campaign.

sentences.zh: 貞元三年，從燧入朝，罷燧兵權，德宗欲以自良代燧。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhenyuan, following Sui to enter court, Sui's military authority was removed; Dezong wished to have Ziliang replace Sui.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zhenyuan (787) Ziliang accompanied Ma Sui to the capital. The emperor stripped Sui of his command and intended to install Ziliang in his place.

sentences.zh: 自良懇辭事燧久，不欲代為軍帥，物議多之，乃授右龍武大將軍。

translations.literal: Ziliang earnestly declined, having served Sui long and not wishing to replace him as army commander; public discussion greatly praised this, and he was then appointed Right General of the Majestic Dragon Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Ziliang declined firmly, saying he had served under Ma Sui too long to take his command. Public opinion applauded his loyalty, and the court appointed him Right General of the Majestic Dragon Guard instead.

sentences.zh: 德宗以河東密邇胡戎，難於擇帥，翌日，自良謝，上謂之曰：「卿於馬燧存軍中事分，誠為得禮，然北門之寄，無易於卿。

translations.literal: Dezong, because Hedong was close to the Hu and Rong and it was difficult to choose a commander, the next day when Ziliang thanked him the emperor said to him: "You in preserving the military division of affairs with Ma Sui have truly obtained propriety, yet the charge of the Northern Gate has no substitute easier than you."
translations.idiomatic: Hedong lay close to the northern frontier, and finding a suitable commander proved difficult. The next day, when Ziliang came to decline again, the emperor told him, "Your regard for Ma Sui's standing is proper, but for guarding the northern gate there is no one I would trust sooner than you."

sentences.zh: 」即日拜檢校工部尚書、兼御史大夫、太原尹、北都留守、河東節度支度營田觀察使。

translations.literal: That same day he was appointed Acting Minister of Works, concurrently Censor-in-Chief, Intendant of Taiyuan, Defender of the Northern Capital, and Military Governor of Hedong with authority over supplies, farming, and observation.
translations.idiomatic: That same day he received appointment as Acting Minister of Works, concurrent Censor-in-Chief, Intendant of Taiyuan, Defender of the Northern Capital, and Military Governor of Hedong with full civil and military authority.

sentences.zh: 在鎮九年，以簡儉守職，軍民胥悅。

translations.literal: He was at his command for nine years, holding his post with simplicity and frugality; soldiers and civilians alike were pleased.
translations.idiomatic: He governed the region for nine years, administering with frugality and discipline, and won the satisfaction of both troops and populace.

sentences.zh: 雖出身戎伍，動必循法，略不以暴戾加人。

translations.literal: Although he came from the military ranks, in action he always followed law, and scarcely imposed violence or cruelty on people.
translations.idiomatic: Though he had risen through the ranks as a soldier, he conducted himself by the book and rarely resorted to harsh or arbitrary punishment.

sentences.zh: 十一年五月，卒於軍，年六十三，上甚嗟惜之，廢朝一日，贈左僕射，賻布帛米粟有差。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the eleventh year he died in the army, age sixty-three; the emperor greatly sighed and regretted this, suspended court for one day, posthumously enfeoffed him as Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, and granted funeral gifts of cloth, silk, rice, and grain in graded amounts.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the eleventh year (795) he died in camp at the age of sixty-three. The emperor mourned him deeply, suspended court for a day, posthumously appointed him Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, and granted graded funeral gifts of cloth, silk, rice, and grain.

sentences.zh: 李説李説，淮安王神通之裔也。

translations.literal: Li Yue—Li Yue was a descendant of Prince Huai'an Li Shentong.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yue was a descendant of Prince Huai'an Li Shentong.

sentences.zh: 父遇，天寶中為御史中丞。

translations.literal: His father Yu, in the Tianbao era served as Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: His father Li Yu had served as Vice Censor-in-Chief during the Tianbao reign.

sentences.zh: 説以門廕歷仕，累佐使幕。

translations.literal: Yue through hereditary privilege passed through offices, and repeatedly assisted on governors' staffs.
translations.idiomatic: Yue entered government by hereditary privilege and served on several governors' staffs in succession.

sentences.zh: 馬燧為河陽三城、太原節度，皆辟為從事。

translations.literal: When Ma Sui was Military Governor of the Three Cities of Heyang and of Taiyuan, he in each case summoned Yue as aide.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Ma Sui held command—first at the Three Cities of Heyang, then at Taiyuan—he recruited Yue to his staff.

sentences.zh: 累轉御史郎官，御史中丞，太原少尹，出為汾州刺史。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly transferred among censorial secretary posts, Vice Censor-in-Chief, Vice Intendant of Taiyuan, and went out as Prefect of Fenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through censorial posts to Vice Censor-in-Chief and Vice Intendant of Taiyuan, then was sent out as Prefect of Fenzhou.

sentences.zh: 節度使李自良復奏為太原少尹、檢校庶子、兼中丞。

translations.literal: The Military Governor Li Ziliang again memorialized to appoint him Vice Intendant of Taiyuan, Acting Chamberlain for the Heir Apparent, and concurrently Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Ziliang became military governor, he had Yue recalled as Vice Intendant of Taiyuan, Acting Chamberlain for the Heir Apparent, and concurrent Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 貞元十一年五月，自良病，凡六日而卒。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the eleventh year of Zhenyuan, Ziliang fell ill; after six days in all he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the eleventh year of Zhenyuan (795), Ziliang fell ill and died six days later.

sentences.zh: 匿喪，陽言病甚，數日發喪。

translations.literal: They concealed the mourning, falsely declared his illness severe, and after several days announced the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: Yue and his allies concealed the death, publicly claiming Ziliang was gravely ill, and only announced the funeral several days later.

sentences.zh: 先是，都虞候張瑤久在軍，素得士心，嘗請假遷葬，自良未許。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Chief Army Inspector Zhang Yao had long been in the army and by nature won the hearts of the troops; he once requested leave to relocate a burial, and Ziliang had not granted it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yao, the army's chief inspector, had long served in the command and enjoyed the troops' loyalty. He had once asked leave to rebury a relative, which Ziliang had refused.

sentences.zh: 至是，説與監軍王定遠謀，乃給瑤假，以大將毛朝陽代瑤，然後遣使告自良病。

translations.literal: At this time Yue together with the Army Supervisor Wang Dingyuan plotted; they then granted Yao leave, replaced Yao with the great general Mao Chaoyang, and afterward sent envoys to report that Ziliang was ill.
translations.idiomatic: Yue conspired with the army supervisor Wang Dingyuan. They granted Zhang Yao his leave, installed the general Mao Chaoyang in his post, and only then sent word that Ziliang had fallen ill.

sentences.zh: 中使第五國珍自雲、朔使還，過太原，聞自良病，中使遲留信宿。

translations.literal: The palace envoy Diwu Guozhen, returning from a mission to Yun and Shuo, passed through Taiyuan, heard that Ziliang was ill, and the palace envoy delayed and stayed two nights.
translations.idiomatic: The palace envoy Diwu Guozhen was returning from a mission to Yun and Shuo when he passed through Taiyuan, heard that Ziliang was ill, and lingered two nights.

sentences.zh: 自良卒，國珍急馳至京，先説使至。

translations.literal: When Ziliang died, Guozhen urgently galloped to the capital; Yue's envoy arrived first.
translations.idiomatic: When Ziliang died, Guozhen raced to the capital—but Yue's messenger had already arrived ahead of him.

sentences.zh: 乃下制以通王領河東節度大使，以説為行軍司馬，充節度留後、北都副留守；

translations.literal: Then an edict was issued appointing the Prince of Tong to head the Hedong Military Governorship, and Yue as Campaigning Army Marshal, filling the post of Military Governor's Acting Deputy and Vice Defender of the Northern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: The court issued orders appointing the Prince of Tong nominal military governor of Hedong, with Li Yue as campaigning army marshal, acting military governor, and Vice Defender of the Northern Capital.

sentences.zh: 仍令國珍齎説官告及軍府將吏部內刺史等敕書三十余通往太原宣賜，軍中始定。

translations.literal: He was still ordered to have Guozhen carry Yue's commission of appointment and more than thirty edicts for army headquarters generals, clerks, and prefects within the ministry, going to Taiyuan to proclaim and bestow them; the army then first settled.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhen was sent back to Taiyuan bearing Yue's commission and more than thirty edicts appointing headquarters officers and prefects. Once these were proclaimed, the army quieted.

sentences.zh: 定遠恃立説之功，頗恣縱橫，軍政皆自專決，仍請賜印。

translations.literal: Dingyuan relied on the merit of establishing Yue, was rather unrestrained and arbitrary, and military and civil affairs were all decided by himself alone; he still requested the bestowal of a seal.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dingyuan, claiming credit for putting Yue in power, grew arrogant and took sole charge of military and civil affairs. He even petitioned for an official seal.

sentences.zh: 監軍有印，自定遠始也。

translations.literal: Army supervisors having seals began from Dingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: The practice of issuing seals to army supervisors began with Dingyuan.

sentences.zh: 定遠既得印，益暴，將吏輒自補授，説浸不歡，遂成嫌隙。

translations.literal: Once Dingyuan obtained the seal he became still more violent; generals and clerks were promptly self-appointed and supplemented, Yue gradually became displeased, and thus a rift of suspicion was formed.
translations.idiomatic: Once he held the seal, Dingyuan grew still more brutal, appointing officers on his own authority. Yue's displeasure deepened, and enmity grew between them.

sentences.zh: 是歲七月，定遠署虞候田宏為列將，以代彭令茵。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of that year Dingyuan appointed the Army Inspector Tian Hong as a ranked general, to replace Peng Lingyin.
translations.idiomatic: That seventh month Dingyuan named the army inspector Tian Hong a ranked general to replace Peng Lingyin.

sentences.zh: 令茵不伏，揚言曰：「超補列將，非功不可，宏有何功，敢代予任！

translations.literal: Lingyin would not submit, and proclaimed aloud: "Supernumerary appointment to ranked general—without merit it cannot be done; what merit does Hong have, that he dares replace my post!"
translations.idiomatic: Peng Lingyin refused to accept the change and declared openly, "Promotion to ranked general requires real merit. What has Hong done to take my place?"

sentences.zh: 」定遠聞而含怒，召令茵斬之，埋於馬糞之中。

translations.literal: Dingyuan heard this and harbored anger; he summoned Lingyin and beheaded him, burying him in horse dung.
translations.idiomatic: Dingyuan, enraged, had Lingyin summoned and executed, then buried the body in a heap of horse manure.

sentences.zh: 家人請屍，不與，三軍皆怨。

translations.literal: The family requested the corpse; it was not given, and the Three Armies all resented this.
translations.idiomatic: When his family asked for the body, Dingyuan refused. Resentment spread through the entire command.

sentences.zh: 説具以事聞。

translations.literal: Yue fully reported the matter to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Yue reported the entire affair to the throne.

sentences.zh: 德宗以定遠有奉天扈從之功，恕死停任。

translations.literal: Dezong, because Dingyuan had the merit of following in attendance at Fengtian, pardoned him from death and suspended his appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Because Dingyuan had accompanied the emperor to Fengtian, Dezong spared his life and merely suspended him from office.

sentences.zh: 制未至，定遠怒説奏聞，趨府謀殺説，升堂未坐，抽刀刺説，説走而獲免。

translations.literal: Before the edict arrived, Dingyuan was angry that Yue had memorialized and reported; he rushed to the headquarters intending to kill Yue, ascended the hall without yet sitting, drew his knife and stabbed at Yue—Yue fled and escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Before the edict arrived, Dingyuan, furious at Yue's report, rushed to headquarters to kill him. He burst into the hall, drew his blade, and lunged at Yue, who fled and survived.

sentences.zh: 定遠馳至府門，召集將吏，於箱中陳敕牒官告二十余軸，示諸將曰：「有敕，令李景略知留後，遣説赴京，公等皆有恩命。

translations.literal: Dingyuan galloped to the headquarters gate, summoned generals and clerks, displayed in a chest more than twenty scrolls of edicts and commissions of appointment, and showed the generals, saying: "There is an edict appointing Li Jinglue to know the acting governorship, sending Yue to the capital—you all likewise have gracious appointments."
translations.idiomatic: Dingyuan galloped to the gate, assembled the officers, and produced from a chest more than twenty scrolls of edicts and commissions. He told them, "By imperial order Li Jinglue is to take command, Li Yue is recalled to the capital, and each of you has a new appointment."

sentences.zh: 」指箱中示之，諸將方拜抃，大將馬良輔呼而麾眾曰：「箱中皆監軍舊官告，非恩命也，不可受，但備急變爾。

translations.literal: He pointed into the chest to show them; the generals were just bowing in joy when the great general Ma Liangfu called out and commanded the multitude: "In the chest are all the army supervisor's old commissions of appointment—not gracious appointments; you must not accept them, but only prepare for sudden change."
translations.idiomatic: As the officers began to bow in acceptance, the general Ma Liangfu shouted, "Those are Dingyuan's old commissions, not new imperial orders. Do not accept them—he is only preparing a coup."

sentences.zh: 」定遠知事敗，走登乾陽樓，召其部下將卒，多不之應。

translations.literal: Dingyuan knew affairs had failed, fled and ascended the Qianyang Tower, summoned his subordinate generals and soldiers—most did not respond.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing his plot collapse, Dingyuan fled to the Qianyang Tower and called his followers. Few answered.

sentences.zh: 比夜，定遠墜城下槎枿，傷而不死。

translations.literal: By night Dingyuan fell from the timbers beneath the wall, was wounded but did not die.
translations.idiomatic: That night he fell from the wall timbers, injured but alive.

sentences.zh: 尋有詔削奪，長流崖州。

translations.literal: Soon there was an edict stripping his titles, and he was exiled far to Yazhou.
translations.idiomatic: An edict soon stripped his rank and banished him to distant Yazhou.

sentences.zh: 大將高迪等同其謀，説皆斬之。

translations.literal: The great general Gao Di and others shared his plot; Yue had them all beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Yue executed Gao Di and the other conspirators.

sentences.zh: 尋正拜河東節度使，檢校禮部尚書。

translations.literal: Soon he was formally appointed Military Governor of Hedong and Acting Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon formally appointed Military Governor of Hedong and Acting Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 説在鎮六年，初勤心吏職，後遇疾，言語行步蹇澀，不能錄軍府之政，悉監軍主之。

translations.literal: Yue was at his command for six years; at first he was diligent in mind toward clerical duties, but later he encountered illness—speech and gait were obstructed and sluggish, he could not manage the army headquarters' administration, and all was presided over by the army supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: Yue governed for six years. At first he attended diligently to administration, but illness later slowed his speech and gait until he could no longer manage headquarters affairs, which fell entirely to the army supervisor.

sentences.zh: 又為孔目吏宋季等欺誑，軍政事多隳紊，如此累年。

translations.literal: He was again deceived and cheated by the clerical officer Song Ji and others; military and civil affairs were mostly ruined and disordered, like this for successive years.
translations.idiomatic: Clerks such as Song Ji deceived him further, and military administration fell into disorder year after year.

sentences.zh: 十六年十月卒，年六十一，廢朝一日，贈左僕射。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the sixteenth year he died, age sixty-one; court was suspended for one day, and he was posthumously enfeoffed as Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the tenth month of the sixteenth year (800) at the age of sixty-one. The court mourned him for a day and posthumously appointed him Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 是月，制以河東節度行軍司馬鄭儋檢校工部尚書，兼太原尹、御史大夫、河東節度度支營田觀察等使、北都留守，在任不期年而卒。

translations.literal: That month an edict appointed Zheng Dan, Campaigning Army Marshal of Hedong, Acting Minister of Works, concurrently Intendant of Taiyuan, Censor-in-Chief, Commissioner for supplies, farming, and observation of the Hedong Military Governorship, and Defender of the Northern Capital; he was in office less than a full year when he died.
translations.idiomatic: That same month Zheng Dan, campaigning marshal of Hedong, was appointed Acting Minister of Works, Intendant of Taiyuan, Censor-in-Chief, and full military governor with civil authority. He died in office before a year had passed.

sentences.zh: 嚴綬嚴綬，蜀人。

translations.literal: Yan Shou—Yan Shou was a native of Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Shou was a native of Shu.

sentences.zh: 曾祖方約，利州司功。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Fangyue was Director of Merit in Lizhou.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Fangyue had served as Director of Merit in Lizhou.

sentences.zh: 祖挹之，符離尉。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yizhi was magistrate of Fuli.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yizhi had been magistrate of Fuli.

sentences.zh: 父丹，殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: His father Dan was Attendant Censor within the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: His father Dan had served as Palace Attendant Censor.

sentences.zh: 綬，大曆中登進士第，累佐使府。

translations.literal: Shou, in the Dali era passed the jinshi examination, and repeatedly assisted on governors' staffs.
translations.idiomatic: Shou passed the jinshi examination during the Dali reign and served on several governors' staffs in succession.

sentences.zh: 貞元中，由侍御史充宣歙團練副使，深為其使劉贊委遇，政事多所咨訪。

translations.literal: In the Zhenyuan years, from Attendant Censor he filled the post of Deputy Commissioner of the Xuan-She Defense Command, was deeply entrusted and favored by its commissioner Liu Zan, and in government affairs was much consulted and inquired of.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhenyuan he rose from Attendant Censor to deputy commissioner of the Xuan-She defense command, where Governor Liu Zan relied on him heavily and consulted him on most administrative matters.

sentences.zh: 十二年，贊卒，綬掌宣歙留務，傾府藏以進獻，由是有恩，召為尚書刑部員外郎。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year Zan died; Shou took charge of Xuan-She acting duties, emptied the headquarters treasury to present tribute, and thereby gained favor, and was summoned as Vice Director in the Ministry of Justice of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Zan died in the twelfth year (796), Shou took charge of the command, emptied its treasury to send tribute to the court, and was rewarded with appointment as Vice Director in the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 天下賓佐進獻，自綬始也。

translations.literal: Under-Heaven's aides and assistants presenting tribute began from Shou.
translations.idiomatic: The practice of provincial staff sending tribute to the throne began with Shou.

sentences.zh: 未幾，河東節度使李説嬰疾，事多曠弛，行軍司馬鄭儋代綜軍政；

translations.literal: Before long, the Military Governor of Hedong Li Yue suffered chronic illness; affairs were mostly neglected and lax, and the Campaigning Army Marshal Zheng Dan replaced him in overall military and civil government.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Li Yue, military governor of Hedong, fell chronically ill. Affairs languished until the campaigning marshal Zheng Dan took over military administration.

sentences.zh: 既而説卒，因授儋河東節度使。

translations.literal: Before long Yue died, and accordingly Dan was appointed Military Governor of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: When Yue died, Dan was appointed military governor in his place.

sentences.zh: 是時姑息四方諸侯，未嘗特命帥守，物故即用行軍司馬為帥，冀軍情厭伏。

translations.literal: At this time in indulgent appeasement of the four quarters' feudal lords, they never specially appointed commanders and defenders; when one died in office they promptly used the Campaigning Army Marshal as commander, hoping the army's feelings would be satisfied and submissive.
translations.idiomatic: The court was then indulging regional commanders and rarely named outsiders to succeed them. When a governor died, his campaigning marshal was usually promoted, in the hope the army would accept the change.

sentences.zh: 儋既為帥，德宗選朝士可以代儋為行軍司馬者。

translations.literal: Once Dan became commander, Dezong selected a court gentleman who could replace Dan as Campaigning Army Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: With Dan installed as governor, Dezong looked for a court official to replace him as campaigning marshal.

sentences.zh: 因綬前日進獻，上頗記之，故命檢校司封郎中，充河東行軍司馬。

translations.literal: Because Shou had presented tribute the other day, the emperor rather remembered this, and therefore appointed him Acting Director in the Bureau of Enfeoffments, filling the post of Hedong Campaigning Army Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor remembered Shou's recent tribute and appointed him Acting Director in the Bureau of Enfeoffments as campaigning marshal of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 不周歲，儋卒，遷綬銀青光祿大夫、檢校工部尚書，兼太原尹、御中大夫、北都留守，充河東節度支度營田觀察處置等使。

translations.literal: Within less than a full year Dan died; Shou was transferred to Silver-Gleaming Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Acting Minister of Works, concurrently Intendant of Taiyuan, Imperial Censor-in-Chief, Defender of the Northern Capital, and Commissioner for supplies, farming, observation, and disposition of the Hedong Military Governorship.
translations.idiomatic: Less than a year later Dan died, and Shou was promoted to Silver-Gleaming Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Acting Minister of Works, Intendant of Taiyuan, Censor-in-Chief, Defender of the Northern Capital, and full military governor of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 元和元年，楊惠琳叛於夏州，劉辟叛於成都，綬表請出師討伐。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanhe Yang Huilin rebelled at Xiazhou and Liu Pi rebelled at Chengdu; Shou memorialized requesting to march out with troops to suppress and punish them.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yuanhe (806), when Yang Huilin rebelled at Xiazhou and Liu Pi at Chengdu, Shou memorialized offering to lead troops against them.

sentences.zh: 綬悉選精甲，付牙將李光顏兄弟，光顏累立戰功。

translations.literal: Shou selected in full elite armor, entrusted it to the guard officer Li Guangyan and his brother; Guangyan repeatedly established battle achievements.
translations.idiomatic: Shou selected the best troops and entrusted them to his guard officer Li Guangyan and his brother, who won repeated victories on campaign.

sentences.zh: 蜀、夏平，加綬檢校尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: When Shu and Xia were pacified, Shou was additionally appointed Acting Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebellions in Shu and Xia were suppressed, Shou was promoted to Acting Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 尋拜司空，進階金紫，封扶風郡公。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Minister of Works, advanced in rank to Golden Purple, and enfeoffed as Duke of Fufeng Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed Minister of Works, raised to the Golden Purple rank, and enfeoffed as Duke of Fufeng.

sentences.zh: 綬在鎮九年，以寬惠為政，士馬蕃息，境內稱治。

translations.literal: Shou was at his command for nine years, governing with lenience and kindness; soldiers and horses multiplied, and within the borders he was called well governed.
translations.idiomatic: During nine years in command he ruled with lenience and kindness. His forces and herds prospered, and the region was regarded as well governed.

sentences.zh: 四年，入拜尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he entered and was appointed Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was recalled to court as Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 綬雖名家子，為吏有方略，然銳於勢利，不存名節，人士以此薄之。

translations.literal: Although Shou was a son of an eminent family and as an official had strategy and method, yet he was keen on power and profit and did not preserve reputation and integrity; gentlemen therefore held him in light esteem.
translations.idiomatic: Though born to a distinguished house and capable in office, Shou was avid for power and profit and cared little for reputation. Men of standing looked down on him for it.

sentences.zh: 嘗預百僚廊下食，上令中使馬江朝賜櫻桃。

translations.literal: He once participated in the hundred officials' corridor meal; the emperor ordered the palace envoy Ma Jiangchao to bestow cherries.
translations.idiomatic: Once, at a corridor feast for the hundred officials, the emperor sent the palace envoy Ma Jiangchao to distribute cherries.

sentences.zh: 綬居兩班之首，在方鎮時識江朝，敘語次，不覺屈膝而拜，御史大夫高郢亦從而拜。

translations.literal: Shou stood at the head of the two ranks; when in the provinces he had known Jiangchao, and in exchanging words of rank he unconsciously bent his knees and bowed; the Censor-in-Chief Gao Ying likewise followed and bowed.
translations.idiomatic: Shou stood at the head of the civil ranks. Having known Jiangchao from his days in the provinces, he fell into conversation about precedence and, without thinking, knelt and bowed to him. Censor-in-Chief Gao Ying bowed as well.

sentences.zh: 是日，為御史所劾，綬待罪於朝，命釋之。

translations.literal: That day he was impeached by the censors; Shou awaited punishment at court, and an order released him.
translations.idiomatic: That day the censors impeached him. Shou awaited judgment at court, but the emperor ordered him released.

sentences.zh: 翌日，責江朝，降官一等。

translations.literal: The next day Jiangchao was blamed and his office was reduced one grade.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the emperor rebuked Jiangchao and reduced his rank by one grade.

sentences.zh: 尋出鎮荊南，進封鄭國公。

translations.literal: Soon he went out to command Jingnan and was advanced in enfeoffment to Duke of Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon sent out to govern Jingnan and advanced in rank to Duke of Zheng.

sentences.zh: 有漵州蠻首張伯靖者，殺長吏，據辰、錦等州，連九洞以自固，詔綬出兵討之。

translations.literal: There was the Xuzhou barbarian chieftain Zhang Bojing, who killed the chief official, seized Chen, Jin, and other prefectures, linked nine cave-districts to secure himself, and an edict ordered Shou to march out with troops to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: A tribal leader of Xuzhou named Zhang Bojing killed the local prefect, seized Chen, Jin, and neighboring prefectures, and united nine cave districts in his defense. The court ordered Shou to campaign against him.

sentences.zh: 綬遣部將李忠烈齎書曉諭，盡招降之。

translations.literal: Shou sent his subordinate general Li Zhonglie bearing documents to enlighten and instruct them, and completely summoned them to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Shou sent his officer Li Zhonglie with proclamations to win them over, and they all submitted.

sentences.zh: 九年，吳元濟叛，朝議加兵，以綬有弘恕之稱，可委以戎柄，乃授山南東道節度使，尋加淮西招撫使。

translations.literal: In the ninth year Wu Yuanji rebelled; court discussion added troops. Because Shou had the reputation of magnanimity and forbearance, military authority could be entrusted to him; he was then appointed Military Governor of Shannan East Circuit, and soon added Commissioner for Pacification and Recruitment in Huaixi.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year (814) Wu Yuanji rebelled. The court resolved to send more troops. Shou's reputation for magnanimity led the court to entrust him with command, appointing him military governor of Shannan East Circuit and soon adding the title Commissioner for Pacification and Recruitment in Huaixi.

sentences.zh: 綬自帥師壓賊境，無威略以制寇；

translations.literal: Shou himself led the army to press the rebel territory, but had no awe-inspiring strategy to control the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Shou led his army to the rebel border himself but lacked the strategic authority to master the enemy.

sentences.zh: 到軍日，遽發公藏以賞士卒，累年蓄積，一旦而盡。

translations.literal: On the day he reached the army he hastily opened the public treasury to reward the soldiers; accumulations of many years were exhausted in a single day.
translations.idiomatic: On his first day in camp he emptied the public treasury to reward the troops, spending in one day what had been saved over many years.

sentences.zh: 又厚賂中貴人以招聲援。

translations.literal: He again lavishly bribed the palace eunuchs to win vocal support.
translations.idiomatic: He also lavished bribes on palace eunuchs to secure their backing at court.

sentences.zh: 師徒萬余，閉壁而已，經年無尺寸功。

translations.literal: His army of more than ten thousand merely shut the walls; for a full year there was not a fraction of an inch of achievement.
translations.idiomatic: His force of more than ten thousand men simply held their walls. After a full year they had achieved nothing.

sentences.zh: 裴度見上，屢言綬非將帥之才，不可責以戎事，乃拜太子少保代歸。

translations.literal: Pei Du saw the emperor and repeatedly said Shou was not talent for commander and general, and military affairs could not be charged to him; he was then appointed Heir Apparent Junior Tutor to replace him and return.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Du told the emperor repeatedly that Shou lacked the talent of a commander and should not be charged with military affairs. Shou was replaced and recalled as Heir Apparent Junior Tutor.

sentences.zh: 尋檢校司空。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Acting Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed Acting Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 久之，進位太傅，食封至三千戶。

translations.literal: After a long time he was advanced to Grand Tutor, with fief income reaching three thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: In time he was promoted to Grand Tutor with a fief income of three thousand households.

sentences.zh: 長慶二年五月卒，年七十七，詔贈太保。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the second year of Changqing he died, age seventy-seven; an edict posthumously enfeoffed him as Grand Protector.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fifth month of the second year of Changqing (822) at the age of seventy-seven. The court posthumously appointed him Grand Protector.

sentences.zh: 綬材器不逾常品，事兄嫂過謹，為時所稱。

translations.literal: Shou's talent and capacity did not exceed ordinary rank; in serving his elder brother and sister-in-law he was excessively respectful, and was praised by his time.
translations.idiomatic: Shou's abilities were unremarkable, but his scrupulous devotion to his elder brother and sister-in-law won contemporary praise.

sentences.zh: 常以寬柔自持，位躋上公，年至大耋，前後統臨三鎮，皆號雄藩，所親士親睹為將相者凡九人，其貴壽如此。

translations.literal: He constantly maintained himself with lenience and gentleness, his rank ascended to the highest dukes, his years reached great old age; before and after he overall commanded three commands, all called mighty feudatories; among the gentlemen he favored, those who with their own eyes saw become generals and ministers numbered nine in all—his nobility and longevity were like this.
translations.idiomatic: He cultivated a reputation for lenience and lived to great old age, rising to the highest noble rank. He governed three of the empire's mightiest commands in succession, and nine men in his circle rose to become generals or chief ministers. Such were the rewards of his long and privileged career.

sentences.zh: 蕭昕蕭昕，河南人。

translations.literal: Xiao Xin—Xiao Xin was a native of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Xin was a native of Henan.

sentences.zh: 少補崇文進士。

translations.literal: In youth he was selected as a Chongwen jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was selected as a Chongwen jinshi.

sentences.zh: 開元十九年，首舉博學宏辭，授陽武縣主簿。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year of Kaiyuan he was first to pass the Broad Learning and Grand Eloquence examination, and was appointed Chief Clerk of Yangwu County.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year of Kaiyuan (731) he topped the Broad Learning and Grand Eloquence examination and was appointed Chief Clerk of Yangwu County.

sentences.zh: 天寶初，復舉宏辭，授壽安尉，再遷左拾遺。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao he again passed the Grand Eloquence examination, was appointed Wei of Shou'an, and was twice transferred to Left Reminder.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianbao reign he passed the Grand Eloquence examination again, was appointed Defender of Shou'an, and soon promoted to Left Reminder.

sentences.zh: 昕嘗與布衣張鎬友善，館而禮之，表薦之曰：「如鎬者，用之則為王者師，不用則幽谷一叟爾。

translations.literal: Xin once was friendly with the commoner Zhang Hao, lodged and honored him, and in a memorial recommended him, saying: "One like Hao—if employed becomes the king's teacher; if not employed, merely an old man in a secluded valley."
translations.idiomatic: Xin once befriended the commoner Zhang Hao, housed him with honor, and memorialized the throne: "A man like Hao, if used, would be a king's teacher; if passed over, no more than an old man in a secluded valley."

sentences.zh: 」玄宗擢鎬拾遺，不數年，出入將相。

translations.literal: Xuanzong promoted Hao to Reminder; within a few years he entered and exited among generals and ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong appointed Hao Reminder, and within a few years he was moving in and out of the highest civil and military offices.

sentences.zh: 及安祿山反，昕舉贊善大夫來瑱堪任將帥；

translations.literal: When An Lushan rebelled, Xin recommended the Good Companion Lai Tian as capable of filling the post of commander and general.
translations.idiomatic: When An Lushan rebelled, Xin recommended the Good Companion Lai Tian as fit for high command.

sentences.zh: 思明之亂，瑱功居多。

translations.literal: In the rebellion of Sīmíng, Tian's achievements were mostly foremost.
translations.idiomatic: In the campaigns against Shi Siming, Tian accounted for most of the victories.

sentences.zh: 累遷憲部員外郎，為副元帥哥舒翰掌書記。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly transferred to Vice Director in the Bureau of Justice, and served as secretary in charge of documents for the Deputy Commander-in-Chief Geshu Han.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Vice Director in the Bureau of Justice and served as chief secretary to the deputy commander Geshu Han.

sentences.zh: 潼關敗，間道入蜀，遷司門郎中。

translations.literal: When Tong Pass was defeated, he took a bypath into Shu, and was transferred to Director in the Bureau of Gates.
translations.idiomatic: After the defeat at Tong Pass he made his way by hidden routes into Shu and was appointed Director in the Bureau of Gates.

sentences.zh: 尋兼安陸長史，為河南等道都統判官。

translations.literal: Soon he concurrently served as Chief Administrator of Anlu and was judge on the staff of the Commander-in-Chief of Henan and other circuits.
translations.idiomatic: He soon served concurrently as Chief Administrator of Anlu and as judge on the staff of the Henan theater commander.

sentences.zh: 遷中書舍人，兼揚府司馬，佐軍仍舊，入拜本官，累遷秘書監。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Attendant Gentleman at the Secretariat, concurrently Military Aide of Yang Prefecture; assisting the army as before, he entered and received appointment to his original office, and was repeatedly transferred to Director of the Palace Library.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Attendant Gentleman at the Secretariat and concurrently Military Aide of Yang Prefecture. After further service on campaign he returned to court and eventually rose to Director of the Palace Library.

sentences.zh: 代宗幸陜，昕出武關詣行在，轉國子祭酒。

translations.literal: When Emperor Daizong visited Shaan, Xin went out through Wu Pass to the mobile court and was transferred to Chancellor of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Daizong went to Shaan, Xin passed through Wu Pass to join the mobile court and was appointed Chancellor of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 大曆初，持節弔回鶻。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Dali he bore the staff of office to offer condolences to the Uyghurs.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Dali reign he was dispatched with imperial credentials to offer condolences to the Uyghurs.

sentences.zh: 時回鶻恃功，廷詰昕曰：「祿山、思明之亂，非我無以平定，唐國奈何市馬而失信，不時歸價？

translations.literal: At that time the Uyghurs relied on their achievements; in court they interrogated Xin, saying: "The rebellions of Lushan and Siming—without us they could not have been pacified. How does the Tang state buy horses yet break faith, not returning payment on time?"
translations.idiomatic: The Uyghurs, proud of their service, confronted Xin in audience: "The rebellions of An Lushan and Shi Siming could not have been crushed without us. Why does Tang buy our horses yet fail to pay on time?"

sentences.zh: 」眾皆失色。

translations.literal: The multitude all changed color.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang envoys blanched.

sentences.zh: 昕答曰：「國家自平寇難，賞功無絲毫之遺，況鄰國乎！

translations.literal: Xin answered: "The state, since pacifying bandit disasters, in rewarding achievements has not the slightest omission—how much more for a neighboring state!"
translations.idiomatic: Xin replied, "Since pacifying the rebellions the court has rewarded every service without stint—how much more should it honor a neighboring state!"

sentences.zh: 且僕固懷恩，我之叛臣，乃者爾助為亂，聯西戎而犯郊畿；

translations.literal: Moreover Pugu Huai'en was our rebel minister; recently you helped him make rebellion, linking with the Western Rong to invade the suburban domains.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Pugu Huai'en was our rebel subject, yet you aided his revolt and joined the Tibetans in raiding our capital approaches.

sentences.zh: 及吐蕃敗走，回紇悔懼，啟顙乞和。

translations.literal: When the Tibetans were defeated and fled, the Uyghurs repented and feared, bared their foreheads and begged for peace.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tibetans were routed, the Uyghurs were filled with remorse and fear and came begging for peace with foreheads pressed to the ground.

sentences.zh: 非大唐存念舊功，則當匹馬不得出塞矣！

translations.literal: Had not Great Tang preserved regard for old achievements, then not even a single horse should have been allowed out of the frontier passes!
translations.idiomatic: Had Tang not remembered your former service, not a single horse of yours would have been allowed beyond the passes!

sentences.zh: 是回紇自絕，非我失信。

translations.literal: It is the Uyghurs who cut themselves off—not we who broke faith.
translations.idiomatic: It is the Uyghurs who have cut themselves off, not Tang that has broken faith.

sentences.zh: 」回紇慚退，加禮以歸，為常侍。

translations.literal: The Uyghurs withdrew in shame; he was treated with added ceremony on his return and was made Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: The Uyghurs withdrew abashed. Xin returned with added honors and was appointed Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 十二年。

translations.literal: The twelfth year.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year.

sentences.zh: 朱泚之亂，徒步出城，泚急求之，亡竄山谷間。

translations.literal: In the rebellion of Zhu Ci he went out of the city on foot; Ci urgently sought him, and he fled and hid among mountains and valleys.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhu Ci's rebellion he fled the capital on foot. Ci searched for him urgently, and he hid in the mountains.

sentences.zh: 至奉天，遷太子少傅。

translations.literal: When he reached Fengtian he was transferred to Heir Apparent Junior Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: Reaching Fengtian, he was appointed Heir Apparent Junior Tutor.

sentences.zh: 貞元初，兼禮部尚書，尋復知貢舉。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenyuan he concurrently served as Minister of Rites, and soon again supervised the civil service examinations.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhenyuan he was made concurrent Minister of Rites and soon resumed charge of the civil service examinations.

sentences.zh: 五年，致仕。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he retired from office.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he retired.

sentences.zh: 七年，卒於家，年九十，廢朝，諡曰懿。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he died at home, age ninety; court was suspended, and his posthumous title was Yi.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home in the seventh year at the age of ninety. Court was suspended for mourning, and he was given the posthumous title Yi.

sentences.zh: 杜亞杜亞，字次公，自云京兆人也。

translations.literal: Du Ya—Du Ya, style name Cigong, himself said he was a native of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Du Ya, style name Cigong, claimed descent from Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 少頗涉學，善言物理及歷代成敗之事。

translations.literal: In youth he was rather versed in learning, skilled at speaking of natural principle and the successes and failures of successive dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he studied widely and spoke fluently on practical affairs and the rise and fall of past dynasties.

sentences.zh: 至德初，於靈武獻封章，言政事，授校書郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhide, at Lingwu he presented a sealed memorial discussing government affairs, and was appointed Collator.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhide reign he submitted a sealed memorial on state affairs at Lingwu and was appointed Collator.

sentences.zh: 其年，杜鴻漸為河西節度，辟為從事，累授評事、御史。

translations.literal: That year Du Hongjian was Military Governor of Hexi; he summoned Ya as aide, and repeatedly appointed him Evaluator and Censor.
translations.idiomatic: That same year Du Hongjian became military governor of Hexi and recruited Ya to his staff, promoting him through Evaluator and Censor.

sentences.zh: 後入朝，歷工、戶、兵、吏四員外郎。

translations.literal: Later he entered court and passed through Vice Director posts in the Ministries of Works, Revenue, War, and Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He later entered court and served in succession as Vice Director in the Ministries of Works, Revenue, War, and Personnel.

sentences.zh: 永泰末，劍南叛亂，鴻漸以宰相出領山、劍副元帥，以亞及楊炎並為判官。

translations.literal: At the end of Yongtai Jiannan rebelled; Hongjian as Chancellor went out to head the Shan-Jian Deputy Commander-in-Chief, and made Ya and Yang Yan both judges on his staff.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Yongtai, when Jiannan rebelled, Hongjian went out as chancellor and deputy commander of the Shan-Jian theater, appointing both Ya and Yang Yan as his staff judges.

sentences.zh: 使還，授吏部郎中、諫議大夫。

translations.literal: When the mission returned, he was appointed Director in the Ministry of Personnel and Remonstrance Grandee.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was appointed Director in the Ministry of Personnel and Remonstrance Grandee.

sentences.zh: 炎為禮部郎中、知制誥、中書舍人。

translations.literal: Yan was Director in the Ministry of Rites, drafter of edicts, and Attendant Gentleman at the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yan meanwhile had risen to Director in the Ministry of Rites, drafter of edicts, and Attendant Gentleman at the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 亞自以才用合當柄任，雖為諫議大夫，而心不悅。

translations.literal: Ya himself believed his talent and employment suited him to hold the helm; although he was Remonstrance Grandee, his heart was not pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Ya believed his talents entitled him to the highest office. Though appointed Remonstrance Grandee, he was dissatisfied.

sentences.zh: 李棲筠承恩，眾望必為宰相，亞厚結之。

translations.literal: Li Qiyun received imperial favor; public expectation was certain he would become Chancellor—Ya formed a thick bond with him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Qiyun enjoyed imperial favor and was widely expected to become chancellor. Ya cultivated a close alliance with him.

sentences.zh: 元載得罪，亞與劉晏、李涵等七人同鞫訊之。

translations.literal: When Yuan Zai offended and was guilty, Ya together with Liu Yan, Li Han, and seven others jointly interrogated him.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Zai fell from power, Ya joined Liu Yan, Li Han, and five others in interrogating him.

sentences.zh: 載死之翌日，亞遷給事中、河北宣慰使。

translations.literal: The day after Zai died, Ya was transferred to Attendant Gentleman and Commissioner to Console Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: The day after Zai's execution Ya was promoted to Attendant Gentleman and Commissioner to Console Hebei.

sentences.zh: 宰相常袞亦不悅亞，歲餘，出為洪州刺史、兼御史中丞、江西都團練觀察使。

translations.literal: The Chancellor Chang Gun also was not pleased with Ya; after more than a year he went out as Prefect of Hongzhou, concurrently Vice Censor-in-Chief, and Commissioner of the Jiangxi Metropolitan Defense and Observation Command.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Chang Gun likewise disliked him. After little more than a year Ya was sent out as Prefect of Hongzhou, concurrent Vice Censor-in-Chief, and commissioner of the Jiangxi defense command.

sentences.zh: 德宗初嗣位，勵精求賢，令中使召亞。

translations.literal: When Dezong first succeeded to the throne, he exerted himself in refinement and sought the worthy, ordering a palace envoy to summon Ya.
translations.idiomatic: When Dezong first ascended the throne he sought to revive governance and ordered a palace envoy to summon Ya.

sentences.zh: 亞自揣必以宰輔見徵，乃促程而進，累路與人言議，語及行宰相事方面，或以公事諮祈，亞皆納之。

translations.literal: Ya himself reckoned he would certainly be summoned as Chancellor and Deputy; he therefore hastened his journey and advanced, along the road repeatedly discussing with people, his words touching on carrying out Chancellor's affairs and regional matters, or some using official business to consult and petition—Ya accepted them all.
translations.idiomatic: Convinced he was to be summoned as chancellor, Ya hurried to the capital. Along the way he discussed affairs of state openly and accepted petitions from those who sought his favor.

sentences.zh: 既至，帝微知之，不悅；

translations.literal: Once he arrived, the emperor slightly learned of this and was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: When he arrived the emperor learned of this and was displeased.

sentences.zh: 又奏對辭旨疏闊，出為陝州觀察使兼轉運使。

translations.literal: Moreover in memorial responses and audience his wording was broad and loose; he was sent out as Military Governor of Shanzhou and concurrently Transport Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: His answers at audience proved vague and unsatisfactory, and he was sent out as governor of Shanzhou and transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 尋遷河中、晉、絳等州防禦觀察使。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Military Governor of the Defense and Observation Command of Hezhong, Jin, Jiang, and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to govern the Hezhong, Jin, and Jiang defense command.

sentences.zh: 楊炎作相，劉晏得罪，亞坐貶睦州刺史。

translations.literal: Yang Yan became Chancellor; Liu Yan offended and was guilty; Ya sat and was demoted to Prefect of Muzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Yan became chancellor and Liu Yan fell, Ya was demoted to Prefect of Muzhou.

sentences.zh: 興元初，召拜刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xingyuan he was summoned and appointed Vice Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Xingyuan era he was recalled and appointed Vice Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 出為揚州長史、兼御史大夫、淮南節度觀察使。

translations.literal: He went out as Chief Administrator of Yangzhou, concurrently Censor-in-Chief, and Military Governor and Observer of Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as Chief Administrator of Yangzhou, concurrent Censor-in-Chief, and military governor of Huainan.

sentences.zh: 時承陳少遊徵稅煩重，奢侈僭濫之後，又新遭王紹亂兵剽掠；

translations.literal: At that time succeeding Chen Shaoyou's taxation was vexatious and heavy; after extravagance and presumptuous excess, they had again newly suffered Wang Shao's rebel troops plundering and robbing.
translations.idiomatic: The region still bore the burden of Chen Shaoyou's heavy taxes and extravagant rule, and had lately been ravaged by the rebel Wang Shao.

sentences.zh: 淮南之人，望亞之至，革刬舊弊，冀以康寧。

translations.literal: The people of Huainan looked to Ya's arrival to reform and eradicate old abuses, hoping thereby for peace and tranquility.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Huainan looked to Ya's arrival to sweep away old abuses and restore peace.

sentences.zh: 亞自以材當公輔之選，而聯出外職，志頗不適，政事多委參佐，招引賓客，談論而已。

translations.literal: Ya himself believed his talent suited selection for Chancellor and Deputy, yet was repeatedly in outer offices; his ambition was rather ill at ease; government affairs were mostly entrusted to aides, and he gathered and drew in guests, merely discussing and talking.
translations.idiomatic: Ya believed himself fit for the highest offices yet found himself repeatedly posted to the provinces. Discontented, he left most administration to his staff and occupied himself with entertaining guests.

sentences.zh: 揚州官河填淤，漕輓堙塞，又僑寄衣冠及工商等多侵衢造宅，行旅擁弊。

translations.literal: Yangzhou's official canals were filled and silted, transport and grain transport were blocked and sealed; moreover sojourning gentry and merchants and artisans and others mostly encroached on thoroughfares to build residences, and travelers were congested and obstructed.
translations.idiomatic: Yangzhou's canals were silted up and transport choked. Sojourning officials, merchants, and artisans had built houses across the thoroughfares, crowding travelers.

sentences.zh: 亞乃開拓疏啟，公私悅賴，而盛為奢侈。

translations.literal: Ya then opened and expanded dredging and clearing; public and private were pleased and relied on this, yet he greatly practiced extravagance.
translations.idiomatic: Ya dredged and cleared the waterways to general relief, yet indulged himself in lavish display.

sentences.zh: 江南風俗，春中有競渡之戲，方舟並進，以急趨疾進者為勝。

translations.literal: Jiangnan custom in spring had the sport of competitive crossing; paired boats advanced together, and those who hurried and advanced swiftly were victors.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiangnan custom, spring brought boat-racing festivals in which paired boats raced and the swiftest won.

sentences.zh: 亞乃令以漆塗船底，貴其速進；

translations.literal: Ya then ordered the boat bottoms painted with lacquer, valuing their swift advance.
translations.idiomatic: Ya had the boat bottoms lacquered to make them faster.

sentences.zh: 又為綺羅之服，塗之以油，令舟子衣之，入水而不濡。

translations.literal: He also made robes of fine silk, coated them with oil, ordered the boatmen to wear them, and entering water they were not soaked.
translations.idiomatic: He also had fine silk garments oiled so the boatmen could wear them in the water without getting wet.

sentences.zh: 亞本書生，奢縱如此，朝廷亟聞之。

translations.literal: Ya was originally a scholar; to be extravagant and unrestrained like this—the court quickly heard of it.
translations.idiomatic: A scholar by origin, Ya had become so extravagant that reports soon reached the court.

sentences.zh: 貞元五年，以戶部侍郎竇覦為淮南節度代亞。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Zhenyuan, Vice Minister of Revenue Dou Xian was made Military Governor of Huainan to replace Ya.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Zhenyuan (789) Dou Xian, Vice Minister of Revenue, was appointed military governor of Huainan to replace him.

sentences.zh: 亞猶以舊望，竇覦甚畏之。

translations.literal: Ya still relied on his old prestige; Dou Xian greatly feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Ya still carried his former prestige, and Dou Xian stood in awe of him.

sentences.zh: 改檢校吏部尚書，判東都尚書省事，充東都留守、都防禦使。

translations.literal: He was changed to Acting Minister of Personnel, judged the Eastern Capital Secretariat affairs, and filled the posts of Defender of the Eastern Capital and Metropolitan Defense Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned as Acting Minister of Personnel, head of the Eastern Capital secretariat, Defender of the Eastern Capital, and metropolitan defense commissioner.

sentences.zh: 既病風，尚建利以固寵，奏請開苑內地為營田，以資軍糧；

translations.literal: Already afflicted with wind illness, he still sought profit to secure favor, memorializing to request opening lands within the imperial park as military farms to supply army grain.
translations.idiomatic: Though stricken with illness, he still sought profit to secure favor and memorialized to open imperial parklands as military farms to supply army grain.

sentences.zh: 減度支每年所給，從之。

translations.literal: The annual allotment from the Department of Public Works was reduced, and this was followed.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved his plan and reduced the annual allotment from the Department of Public Works.

sentences.zh: 亞不躬親部署，但委判官張薦、楊晪。

translations.literal: Ya did not personally oversee deployment, but only entrusted it to his judges Zhang Jian and Yang Tian.
translations.idiomatic: Ya did not oversee the project himself but left it to his staff judges Zhang Jian and Yang Tian.

sentences.zh: 初，奏請取荒地營田，其苑內地堪耕食者，先為留司中官及軍人等開墾已盡。

translations.literal: At first, in memorializing to take wasteland for military farms, the park lands within suitable for cultivation and food had already been fully opened and reclaimed beforehand by retained-office palace officials and soldiers and others.
translations.idiomatic: When he petitioned to open wasteland for military farms, the cultivable parklands had already been seized and farmed by palace officials and soldiers.

sentences.zh: 晉計急，乃取軍中雜錢舉息與畿內百姓，每至田收之際，多令軍人車牛散入村鄉，收斂百姓所得菽粟將還軍。

translations.literal: Tian's accounts were urgent; he then took miscellaneous army funds and lent them at interest to commoners within the capital region. Each time at harvest season he mostly ordered soldiers with carts and oxen to scatter into villages and hamlets, collecting the grain the commoners had obtained and bringing it back to the army.
translations.idiomatic: Pressed for funds, Yang Tian lent army money at interest to peasants near the capital. At harvest he sent soldiers through the villages to seize the grain and haul it back to camp.

sentences.zh: 民家略盡，無可輸稅，人多艱食，由是大致流散。

translations.literal: Common households were nearly exhausted; there was nothing to submit in tax; many people had difficult food—thereby large numbers mostly scattered and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Households were stripped bare, unable to pay taxes or feed themselves, and the population largely fled.

sentences.zh: 乃厚賂中官，令奏河南尹無政，亞自此亦規求兼領河南尹，事不果。

translations.literal: He then lavishly bribed palace eunuchs to have them memorialize that the Intendant of Henan was without government; from this Ya also schemed to seek concurrent charge of Intendant of Henan—the matter did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: He bribed palace eunuchs to denounce the Intendant of Henan as incompetent, hoping thereby to seize that post himself, but the scheme failed.

sentences.zh: 帝漸知虛誕，乃以禮部尚書董晉代為東都留守，召亞還京師。

translations.literal: The emperor gradually learned of the emptiness and falsehood; he then made Minister of Rites Dong Jin replace him as Defender of the Eastern Capital and summoned Ya back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor gradually learned the truth and replaced him with Minister of Rites Dong Jin as Defender of the Eastern Capital, recalling Ya to the capital.

sentences.zh: 既風疾漸深，又患腳膝，不任朝謁。

translations.literal: Already his wind illness gradually deepened, and he also suffered in feet and knees, unable to bear court audience.
translations.idiomatic: His illness worsened and his legs failed him, leaving him unable to attend court.

sentences.zh: 貞元十四年卒於家，年七十四，贈太子少傅。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Zhenyuan he died at home, age seventy-four, and was posthumously enfeoffed as Heir Apparent Junior Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home in the fourteenth year of Zhenyuan (798) at the age of seventy-four and was posthumously appointed Heir Apparent Junior Tutor.

sentences.zh: 王緯王緯，字文卿，太原人也。

translations.literal: Wang Wei—Wang Wei, style name Wenqing, was a native of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wei, style name Wenqing, was a native of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 祖景，司門員外、萊州刺史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Jing was Vice Director in the Bureau of Gates and Prefect of Laizhou.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Jing had served as Vice Director in the Bureau of Gates and Prefect of Laizhou.

sentences.zh: 父之咸，長安尉；

translations.literal: His father Zhixian was Defender of Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhixian had been Defender of Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 與昆弟之賁、之渙皆善屬文。

translations.literal: Together with his brothers Zhiben and Zhihuan he was all skilled at literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: He and his brothers Zhiben and Zhihuan were all accomplished writers.

sentences.zh: 之咸以緯貴，故累贈刺史。

translations.literal: Because Zhixian was ennobled through Wei, he was repeatedly posthumously enfeoffed as Prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Zhixian was repeatedly posthumously promoted to prefect on account of Wei's eminence.

sentences.zh: 緯舉明經，又書判入等，歷長安尉，出佐使府，授御史郎官，入朝為金部員外郎、劍南租庸使、檢校司封郎中、彭州刺史、檢校庶子、兼御史中丞、西川節度營田副使。

translations.literal: Wei passed the Mingjing examination, and also in document judgment entered the grade; he passed through Defender of Chang'an, went out to assist on a governor's staff, was appointed censorial secretary, entered court as Vice Director in the Bureau of the Treasury, Commissioner for Tax and Corvée in Jiannan, Acting Director in the Bureau of Enfeoffments, Prefect of Pengzhou, Acting Chamberlain for the Heir Apparent, concurrently Vice Censor-in-Chief, and Deputy Commissioner for Military Farms of the Xichuan Military Governorship.
translations.idiomatic: Wei passed the Mingjing examination and ranked in the document-judgment category. He served as Defender of Chang'an, on governors' staffs, and in censorial posts before entering court as Vice Director in the Bureau of the Treasury, Commissioner for Tax and Corvée in Jiannan, Acting Director in the Bureau of Enfeoffments, Prefect of Pengzhou, Acting Chamberlain for the Heir Apparent, concurrent Vice Censor-in-Chief, and deputy commissioner for military farms in Xichuan.

sentences.zh: 初，大曆中，路嗣恭為江西觀察使，陷害判官李泌，將誅之；

translations.literal: Earlier, in the Dali era Lu Sigong was Military Governor of Jiangxi, framed and trapped the judge Li Mi, and was about to execute him.
translations.idiomatic: During the Dali era, when Lu Sigong was governor of Jiangxi, he framed his staff judge Li Mi and was about to have him executed.

sentences.zh: 緯亦為路嗣恭判官，説諭救解，獲免。

translations.literal: Wei also was Lu Sigong's judge; he persuaded and instructed to rescue and release him, and Mi was spared.
translations.idiomatic: Wei, who also served on Sigong's staff, persuaded him to relent, and Mi was spared.

sentences.zh: 貞元三年，泌為相，擢授緯給事中。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhenyuan Mi became Chancellor and promoted Wei to Attendant Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zhenyuan (787), when Mi became chancellor, he promoted Wei to Attendant Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 未數日，又擢為潤州刺史、兼御史中丞、浙江西道都團練觀察使。

translations.literal: Within a few days he was again promoted to Prefect of Runzhou, concurrently Vice Censor-in-Chief, and Commissioner of the Zhejiang West Metropolitan Defense and Observation Command.
translations.idiomatic: Within days he was further promoted to Prefect of Runzhou, concurrent Vice Censor-in-Chief, and commissioner of the Zhejiang West defense command.

sentences.zh: 十年，加御史大夫，兼諸道鹽鐵轉運使。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was added Censor-in-Chief and concurrently Commissioner for Salt and Iron Transport of all circuits.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was made Censor-in-Chief and concurrent commissioner for salt and iron transport on all circuits.

sentences.zh: 三歲，加檢校工部尚書。

translations.literal: After three years he was added Acting Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Three years later he was appointed Acting Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 緯性勤儉，歷官清潔，而傷於苛碎，多用削刻之吏，督察巡屬，人不聊生。

translations.literal: Wei's nature was diligent and frugal; in successive offices he was clean and pure, yet he was harmed by harsh minuteness, mostly using harsh and cutting clerks, supervising and inspecting subordinates on tour, and people could not sustain life.
translations.idiomatic: Wei was diligent and frugal and maintained a clean record in office, but he was excessively meticulous, employing harsh subordinates who hounded his jurisdictions until the people could scarcely live.

sentences.zh: 貞元十四年卒，年七十一，廢朝一日，贈太子少保。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Zhenyuan he died, age seventy-one; court was suspended for one day, and he was posthumously enfeoffed as Heir Apparent Junior Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fourteenth year of Zhenyuan (798) at the age of seventy-one. The court mourned him for a day and posthumously appointed him Heir Apparent Junior Tutor.

sentences.zh: 李若初李若初，趙郡人。

translations.literal: Li Ruochu—Li Ruochu was a native of Zhao Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ruochu was a native of Zhao Commandery.

sentences.zh: 貞觀中并州長史、工部侍郎弘節之曾孫也。

translations.literal: He was the great-grandson of Hongjie, Chief Administrator of Bingzhou and Vice Minister of Works in the Zhenguan era.
translations.idiomatic: He was the great-grandson of Hongjie, who had served as Chief Administrator of Bingzhou and Vice Minister of Works under Emperor Taizong.

sentences.zh: 祖道謙，太府卿。

translations.literal: His grandfather Daoqian was Director of the Palace Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Daoqian had been Director of the Palace Treasury.

sentences.zh: 若初少孤貧，初為轉運使劉晏下微冗散職；

translations.literal: Ruochu in youth was orphaned and poor; at first he held a minor redundant post under the Transport Commissioner Liu Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned and poor in youth, Ruochu began in a minor post on the staff of Transport Commissioner Liu Yan.

sentences.zh: 晏判官包佶重其勤幹，以女妻之。

translations.literal: Yan's judge Bao Ji valued his diligence and capability and gave him his daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Yan's staff judge Bao Ji admired his diligence and gave him his daughter in marriage.

sentences.zh: 歷陳州太康令。

translations.literal: He passed through Magistrate of Taikang in Chenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Magistrate of Taikang in Chen Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 刺史李芃初蒞官，若初獻計，請收斂羨余錢物，交結權貴，芃厚遇之。

translations.literal: When Prefect Li Peng first assumed office, Ruochu presented a plan requesting to collect surplus funds and goods, form connections with powerful nobles, and Peng treated him generously.
translations.idiomatic: When Prefect Li Peng first took office, Ruochu proposed collecting surplus funds and cultivating ties with the powerful. Peng favored him generously.

sentences.zh: 累歲，芃遷河陽三城使，奏若初為從事，軍中之事，多以委之。

translations.literal: Over successive years Peng was transferred to Commissioner of the Three Cities of Heyang; he memorialized to appoint Ruochu as aide, and army affairs were mostly entrusted to him.
translations.idiomatic: After several years Peng was transferred to command the Three Cities of Heyang and had Ruochu appointed to his staff, entrusting him with most military affairs.

sentences.zh: 累授檢校郎中、兼中丞、懷州刺史。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly appointed Acting Director, concurrently Vice Censor-in-Chief, and Prefect of Huaizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through Acting Director, concurrent Vice Censor-in-Chief, and Prefect of Huaizhou.

sentences.zh: 轉虢州刺史，坐公事為觀察使劾奏，免歸。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Prefect of Guozhou; for an official matter he was impeached and memorialized by the Military Governor, was dismissed, and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Prefect of Guo Prefecture, he was impeached by his military governor for an official matter and dismissed.

sentences.zh: 久之，出為衢州刺史，遷福州刺史、兼御史中丞、福建都團練使。

translations.literal: After a long time he went out as Prefect of Quzhou, was transferred to Prefect of Fuzhou, concurrently Vice Censor-in-Chief, and Metropolitan Training Commissioner of Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: After a time he was appointed Prefect of Quzhou, then Fuzhou, with concurrent Vice Censor-in-Chief and metropolitan training commissioner of Fujian.

sentences.zh: 尋遷越州刺史、浙江東道都團練觀察使。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Prefect of Yuezhou and Commissioner of the Zhedong Metropolitan Defense and Observation Command.
