translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to Prefect of Yuezhou and commissioner of the Zhedong defense and observation command.

sentences.zh: 十四年秋，代王緯為潤州刺史、兼御史大夫、浙江都團練觀察、諸道鹽鐵轉運使。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the fourteenth year he replaced Wang Wei as Prefect of Runzhou, concurrently Censor-in-Chief, Zhejiang Metropolitan Defense and Observation Commissioner, and Commissioner for Salt and Iron Transport of all circuits.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the fourteenth year he succeeded Wang Wei as Prefect of Runzhou, Censor-in-Chief, Zhejiang defense commissioner, and salt and iron transport commissioner for all circuits.

sentences.zh: 善於吏道，性嚴強，力束斂下，吏人甚畏服。

translations.literal: He was skilled in the way of clerks; his nature was stern and strong, and he forcefully restrained and collected from subordinates—clerks and people greatly feared and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Skilled in administration and stern by nature, he enforced tight control over subordinates, who feared and obeyed him.

sentences.zh: 方整理鹽法，頗有次敘。

translations.literal: He was just then putting the salt laws in order, with considerable sequence and method.
translations.idiomatic: He was then reorganizing the salt laws with considerable success.

sentences.zh: 貞元十五年，遇疾卒，廢朝一日，贈禮部尚書。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Zhenyuan he encountered illness and died; court was suspended for one day, and he was posthumously enfeoffed as Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He fell ill and died in the fifteenth year of Zhenyuan (799). The court mourned for a day and posthumously appointed him Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 于頎于頎，字休明，河南人也。

translations.literal: Yu Yi—Yu Yi, style name Xiuming, was a native of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yi, style name Xiuming, was a native of Henan.

sentences.zh: 父庭謂，濟王府倉曹，累贈尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: His father Tingwei was Warehouse Clerk of the Prince of Ji's establishment; he was repeatedly posthumously enfeoffed as Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: His father Tingwei had been Warehouse Clerk in the establishment of the Prince of Ji and was posthumously promoted to Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 頎少以吏事聞，累授京兆府士曹，為尹史翽所賞重。

translations.literal: Yi in youth was known for clerical affairs; he was repeatedly appointed Clerk of Gentlemen in the Jingzhao Prefecture and was valued and esteemed by the Intendant Shi Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Yi won early notice for administrative skill and rose to Clerk of Gentlemen in Jingzhao, where Intendant Shi Hui valued him highly.

sentences.zh: 翽出鎮襄、漢，奏為御史，充判官。

translations.literal: Hui went out to command Xiang and Han, memorialized to appoint him Censor, and filled the post of judge.
translations.idiomatic: When Hui took command of Xiang and Han, he had Yi appointed Censor and staff judge.

sentences.zh: 翽為亂兵所殺，頎挺出收葬遺骸，時人義之。

translations.literal: Hui was killed by mutinous troops; Yi stepped forward to collect and bury the remains, and people of the time praised his righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: When Hui was killed by mutinous troops, Yi stepped forward to recover and bury his body, an act contemporaries praised as righteous.

sentences.zh: 度支使第五琦署為河東租庸使，累授鳳翔少尹、度支郎中、兼御史中丞、轉運租庸糧料鹽鐵等使。

translations.literal: The Commissioner of Public Works Diwu Qi appointed him Hedong Commissioner for Tax and Corvée; he was repeatedly appointed Vice Intendant of Fengxiang, Director in the Department of Public Works, concurrently Vice Censor-in-Chief, and Commissioner for transport, tax, corvée, grain provisions, salt, iron, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: Commissioner of Public Works Diwu Qi appointed him Hedong tax and corvée commissioner. He rose through Vice Intendant of Fengxiang, Director in the Department of Public Works, Vice Censor-in-Chief, and various transport and supply commissions.

sentences.zh: 頎因奏移轉運汴州院於河陰，以汴州累遇兵亂，散失錢帛故也。

translations.literal: Yi therefore memorialized to move the transport Bianzhou depot to Heyin, because Bianzhou had repeatedly encountered military disorder and scattered and lost money and silk.
translations.idiomatic: Yi memorialized to relocate the transport depot from Bianzhou to Heyin, since Bianzhou had repeatedly suffered military disorder and lost its stores of cash and silk.

sentences.zh: 元載為諸道營田使，又署為郎官，令於東都、汝州開置屯田。

translations.literal: Yuan Zai was Commissioner for Military Farms of all circuits; he again appointed him a secretary and ordered him to open and establish military farms at the Eastern Capital and in Ruzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Zai, commissioner for military farms on all circuits, appointed him a secretary and ordered him to establish farms at the Eastern Capital and in Ru Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 歷戶部侍郎、秘書少監、京兆尹、太府卿，代杜濟為京兆尹。

translations.literal: He passed through Vice Minister of Revenue, Vice Director of the Palace Library, Intendant of Jingzhao, and Director of the Palace Treasury, and replaced Du Ji as Intendant of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Vice Minister of Revenue, Vice Director of the Palace Library, Intendant of Jingzhao, and Director of the Palace Treasury, and replaced Du Ji as Intendant of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 及為大官，好任機數，專候權要，朝列中無勢利者，視之蔑如也。

translations.literal: Once he became a great official, he loved to employ stratagems and schemes, exclusively waiting on the powerful and important; among the court ranks those without power and profit he viewed with contempt.
translations.idiomatic: Once he reached high office he relied on intrigue, courted the powerful, and treated colleagues without influence with open contempt.

sentences.zh: 曲事元載，親昵之。

translations.literal: He bent to serve Yuan Zai and was intimate and close with him.
translations.idiomatic: He curried favor with Yuan Zai and grew close to him.

sentences.zh: 而為政苛細無大體；

translations.literal: Yet in governing he was harsh and minute, without large principles.
translations.idiomatic: In government he was petty and lacked broad vision.

sentences.zh: 丁所生母憂罷。

translations.literal: He observed mourning for his birth mother and left office.
translations.idiomatic: He left office to observe mourning for his birth mother.

sentences.zh: 及載得罪後，出為鄭州刺史，遷河南尹，以無政績代還。

translations.literal: After Zai offended and was guilty, Yi went out as Prefect of Zhengzhou, was transferred to Intendant of Henan, and because he had no administrative achievements was replaced and returned.
translations.idiomatic: After Zai's fall he was sent out as Prefect of Zhengzhou, then Intendant of Henan, and was recalled for lack of achievement.

sentences.zh: 時徵汾州刺史劉暹。

translations.literal: At that time Prefect of Fenzhou Liu Xian was summoned.
translations.idiomatic: The court was then summoning Liu Xian, Prefect of Fenzhou.

sentences.zh: 暹剛腸嫉惡，歷典數州，皆為廉使畏懼。

translations.literal: Xian had a stern disposition and hated evil; in successive governorships of several prefectures, all inspection commissioners feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Xian was stern and incorruptible; in several prefectures he had governed, censorial commissioners feared him.

sentences.zh: 宰相盧杞恐暹為御史大夫，虧沮己之所見，遽稱薦頎為御史大夫，以其柔佞易制也。

translations.literal: The Chancellor Lu Qi feared Xian as Censor-in-Chief would thwart his own views; he hastily praised and recommended Yi as Censor-in-Chief, because he was soft, fawning, and easy to control.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Lu Qi feared that if Liu Xian became Censor-in-Chief he would obstruct Qi's designs. Qi therefore hastily recommended Yi instead, judging him pliable and easy to control.

sentences.zh: 從幸奉天，改左散騎常侍，歷左千牛上將軍，徙大理卿、太子少保、工部尚書。

translations.literal: He followed in fortune to Fengtian, was changed to Left Regular Attendant, passed through Left General of the Thousand-Ox Guard, was moved to Chief Justice, Heir Apparent Junior Tutor, and Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied the emperor to Fengtian and was appointed Left Regular Attendant, then Left General of the Thousand-Ox Guard, Chief Justice, Heir Apparent Junior Tutor, and Minister of Works in succession.

sentences.zh: 因入朝仆地，為金吾仗衛掖起，改太子少師致仕。

translations.literal: Because at court audience he fell prostrate, the Golden Crow guard attendants helped him up; he was changed to Heir Apparent Junior Tutor and retired.
translations.idiomatic: He collapsed during a court audience and was helped up by Golden Crow guards. He was reassigned as Heir Apparent Junior Tutor and retired.

sentences.zh: 貞元十五年卒，時年七十四。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Zhenyuan he died, at the time age seventy-four.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fifteenth year of Zhenyuan (799) at the age of seventy-four.

sentences.zh: 盧徵盧徵，范陽人也，家於鄭之中牟。

translations.literal: Lu Zheng—Lu Zheng was a native of Fanyang, his family residing in Zhongmou in Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zheng was a native of Fanyang whose family had settled in Zhongmou in Zheng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 少涉獵書記。

translations.literal: In youth he dabbled in secretarial work.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he studied secretarial work.

sentences.zh: 永泰中，江淮轉運使劉晏辟為從事，委以腹心之任，累授殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: In Yongtai the Jiang-Huai Transport Commissioner Liu Yan summoned him as aide, entrusted him with tasks of innermost trust, and repeatedly appointed him Attendant Censor within the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: During Yongtai, Transport Commissioner Liu Yan recruited him to his staff, entrusted him with confidential duties, and promoted him to Palace Attendant Censor.

sentences.zh: 晏得罪，貶珍州司戶。

translations.literal: When Yan offended and was guilty, Zheng was demoted to Registrar of Zhenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Yan fell, Zheng was demoted to Registrar of Zhen Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 元琇亦晏之門人，興元中，為戶部侍郎、判度支，薦徵為京兆司錄、度支員外。

translations.literal: Yuan Xiu was also Yan's disciple; in Xingyuan he was Vice Minister of Revenue and judged the Department of Public Works, and recommended Zheng as Jingzhao Registrar and Vice Director in the Department of Public Works.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Xiu, another of Yan's protégés, became Vice Minister of Revenue and head of the Department of Public Works in the Xingyuan era and recommended Zheng as Jingzhao Registrar and Vice Director in that department.

sentences.zh: 琇得罪，坐貶為信州長史。

translations.literal: When Xiu offended and was guilty, Zheng sat and was demoted to Chief Administrator of Xinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiu fell, Zheng was demoted to Chief Administrator of Xin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 遷信州刺史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Prefect of Xinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Prefect of Xin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 入為右司郎中，驟遷給事中。

translations.literal: He entered as Director in the Right Secretariat and was swiftly transferred to Attendant Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court as Director in the Right Secretariat and was soon promoted to Attendant Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 戶部侍郎竇參深遇之，方倚以自代。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of Revenue Dou Can deeply favored him and was just then relying on him to replace himself.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister of Revenue Dou Can favored him deeply and intended to make him his successor.

sentences.zh: 貞元八年春，同州刺史闕，參請以尚書左丞趙憬補之，特詔用徵，以間參腹心也。

translations.literal: In the spring of the eighth year of Zhenyuan the Prefect of Tongzhou post was vacant; Can requested that Left Vice Director of the Secretariat Zhao Jing fill it, but a special edict employed Zheng, to come between Can and his inner circle.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the eighth year of Zhenyuan (792), when the prefecture of Tong was vacant, Can proposed Left Vice Director Zhao Jing for the post, but a special edict appointed Zheng instead, inserting him between Can and his inner circle.

sentences.zh: 數歲，轉華州刺史。

translations.literal: After several years he was transferred to Prefect of Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later he was transferred to Prefect of Hua Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 徵冀復入用，深結托中貴，厚遺之。

translations.literal: Zheng hoped to reenter employment, formed deep bonds with palace eunuchs, and gave them lavish gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Hoping to return to central office, Zheng cultivated palace eunuchs and lavished gifts on them.

sentences.zh: 故事，同、華以近地人貧，每正至端午降誕，所獻甚薄；

translations.literal: By precedent, because Tong and Hua were nearby and the people poor, at each New Year, Dragon Boat Festival, and imperial birthday the offerings presented were very slight.
translations.idiomatic: By custom, because Tong and Hua were near the capital and their populations poor, tribute at New Year, the Dragon Boat Festival, and the emperor's birthday had always been modest.

sentences.zh: 徵遂竭其財賦，每有所進獻，輒加常數，人不堪命。

translations.literal: Zheng then exhausted their wealth and taxes; whenever there was an offering to present, he always added to the usual amount, and people could not bear the command.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng exhausted local resources, exceeding the customary amounts on every tribute occasion until the people could not endure it.

sentences.zh: 疾病臥理者數年，貞元十六年卒，時年六十四。

translations.literal: Ill with disease, he administered from his bed for several years; in the sixteenth year of Zhenyuan he died, at the time age sixty-four.
translations.idiomatic: Ill for years he governed from his bed and died in the sixteenth year of Zhenyuan (800) at the age of sixty-four.

sentences.zh: 楊憑楊憑，字虛受，弘農人。

translations.literal: Yang Ping—Yang Ping, style name Xushou, was a native of Hongnong.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Ping, style name Xushou, was a native of Hongnong.

sentences.zh: 舉進士，累佐使府。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and repeatedly assisted on governors' staffs.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and served on several governors' staffs.

sentences.zh: 徵為監察御史，不樂檢束，遂求免。

translations.literal: He was appointed Investigating Censor but did not enjoy restraint and inspection, and therefore requested to be released.
translations.idiomatic: Appointed Investigating Censor, he disliked its constraints and asked to be relieved.

sentences.zh: 累遷起居舍人、左司員外郎、禮部兵部郎中、太常少卿、湖南江西觀察使，入為左散騎常侍、刑部侍郎、京兆尹。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly transferred to Diary Attendant, Left Secretariat Vice Director, Director in the Ministries of Rites and War, Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, Military Governor of Hunan and Jiangxi, and entered as Left Regular Attendant, Vice Minister of Justice, and Intendant of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through Diary Attendant, Left Secretariat Vice Director, Director in the Ministries of Rites and War, Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and governor of Hunan and Jiangxi before entering court as Left Regular Attendant, Vice Minister of Justice, and Intendant of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 憑工文辭，少負氣節；

translations.literal: Ping was skilled in literary composition and in youth bore moral integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Ping was accomplished in letters and possessed moral resolve from youth.

sentences.zh: 與母弟凝、凌相友愛，皆有時名。

translations.literal: With his younger brothers by the same mother, Ning and Ling, he was mutually friendly and loving; all had renown in their time.
translations.idiomatic: He was close to his younger brothers Ning and Ling, and all three enjoyed contemporary renown.

sentences.zh: 重交遊，尚然諾，與穆質、許孟容、李鄘、王仲舒為友，故時人稱楊、穆、許、李之友，仲舒以後進慕而入焉。

translations.literal: He valued forming friendships and honored keeping promises; with Mu Zhi, Xu Mengrong, Li Yong, and Wang Zhongshu he was friends, so people of the time called them the friends of Yang, Mu, Xu, and Li; Zhongshu as a junior admired them and entered the group.
translations.idiomatic: He valued friendship and kept his word. With Mu Zhi, Xu Mengrong, Li Yong, and Wang Zhongshu he formed a celebrated circle known as the friends of Yang, Mu, Xu, and Li; Zhongshu joined them as a junior admirer.

sentences.zh: 性尚簡傲，不能接下，以此人多怨之。

translations.literal: His nature favored simplicity and arrogance; he could not accommodate subordinates, and for this many people resented him.
translations.idiomatic: Proud and aloof by nature, he treated subordinates coldly, and many resented him for it.

sentences.zh: 及歷二鎮，尤事奢侈。

translations.literal: Once he had governed two commands, he especially practiced extravagance.
translations.idiomatic: Once he governed two commands, his extravagance grew still worse.

sentences.zh: 元和四年，拜京兆尹，為御史中丞李夷簡劾奏憑前為江西觀察使贓罪及他不法事，敕付御史臺覆按，刑部尚書李鄘、大理卿趙昌同鞫問臺中。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yuanhe he was appointed Intendant of Jingzhao; Vice Censor-in-Chief Li Yijian impeached and memorialized Ping's earlier crimes of embezzlement as Military Governor of Jiangxi and other unlawful matters; an edict entrusted the case to the Censorate for review and investigation, and Minister of Justice Li Yong and Chief Justice Zhao Chang jointly interrogated at the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Yuanhe (809) he was appointed Intendant of Jingzhao. Vice Censor-in-Chief Li Yijian impeached him for embezzlement and other offenses from his days as governor of Jiangxi. The case was referred to the Censorate, with Minister of Justice Li Yong and Chief Justice Zhao Chang conducting the inquiry.

sentences.zh: 又捕得憑前江西判官、監察御史楊瑗系於臺，復命大理少卿胡珦、左司員外郎胡證、侍御史韋顗同推鞫之。

translations.literal: They also captured Ping's former Jiangxi judge and Investigating Censor Yang Yuan and bound him at the Censorate; they again ordered Vice Chief Justice Hu Xing, Left Secretariat Vice Director Hu Zheng, and Attendant Censor Wei Yi jointly to press and interrogate him.
translations.idiomatic: Ping's former Jiangxi staff judge Yang Yuan was also arrested. Vice Chief Justice Hu Xing, Left Secretariat Vice Director Hu Zheng, and Attendant Censor Wei Yi were ordered to interrogate him jointly.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「楊憑頃在先朝，委以藩鎮，累更選用，位列大官。

translations.literal: The edict said: "Yang Ping not long ago in the former court was entrusted with a feudal command, repeatedly changed in selection and employment, and ranked among great officials."
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared, "Yang Ping was not long ago entrusted with a provincial command under the former emperor and rose to high rank."

sentences.zh: 近者憲司奏劾，暴揚前事，計錢累萬，曾不報聞，蒙蔽之罪，於何逃責？

translations.literal: Recently the censorial office memorialized impeachment, exposing and proclaiming former matters; the money counted in tens of thousands, yet he never reported and informed—the crime of concealment, how can he escape blame?
translations.idiomatic: The censorate has now exposed his past conduct: wealth amounting to tens of thousands that he never reported. How can he escape the charge of concealment?

sentences.zh: 又營建居室，制度過差，侈靡之風，傷我儉德。

translations.literal: Moreover he built and constructed dwellings; the regulations exceeded proper measure; the wind of extravagance injures our frugal virtue.
translations.idiomatic: He also built residences beyond proper scale, indulging extravagance that offends the court's frugal virtue.

sentences.zh: 以其自尹京邑，人頗懷之，將議刑書，是加憫惻。

translations.literal: Because he himself had been Intendant of the capital region and the people rather cherished him, when about to deliberate the penal code, compassion was added.
translations.idiomatic: Because he had lately governed the capital and retained some public goodwill, the court showed mercy when sentencing.

sentences.zh: 宜從遐譴，以誡百僚，可守賀州臨賀縣尉同正，仍馳驛發遣。

translations.literal: He should follow distant punishment to warn the hundred officials; he may hold Defender of Linhe County in Hezhou with concurrent regular status, and still be dispatched by express relay.
translations.idiomatic: He is banished to serve as Defender of Linhe County in He Prefecture, with rank retained in name only, and is to be sent off at once by relay post.

sentences.zh: 」先是，憑在江西，夷簡自御史出，官在巡屬。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Ping was in Jiangxi, Yijian had come out from the Censors; his office was among touring subordinates.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Ping governed Jiangxi, Yijian had served there as a touring censor under his command.

sentences.zh: 憑頗疏縱，不顧接之。

translations.literal: Ping was rather lax and unrestrained and did not deign to receive him.
translations.idiomatic: Ping treated him with negligent disdain and refused his acquaintance.

sentences.zh: 夷簡常切齒。

translations.literal: Yijian often ground his teeth.
translations.idiomatic: Yijian nursed bitter resentment.

sentences.zh: 及憑歸朝，修第於永寧里，功作並興，又廣蓄妓妾於永樂里之別宅，時人大以為言。

translations.literal: When Ping returned to court he built a mansion in Yongning Ward; construction works rose together, and he also broadly stored singing girls and concubines in a separate residence in Yongle Ward—people of the time greatly spoke of this.
translations.idiomatic: When Ping returned to court he built a mansion in Yongning Ward and kept a large household of entertainers in a separate residence in Yongle Ward, drawing widespread criticism.

sentences.zh: 夷簡乘眾議，舉劾前事，且言修營之僭，將欲殺之。

translations.literal: Yijian seized on public discussion, raised impeachment of former matters, and moreover spoke of the presumption in building and construction, intending to have him killed.
translations.idiomatic: Yijian seized on public outrage to impeach Ping for past crimes and presumptuous building, intending at first to have him executed.

sentences.zh: 及下獄，置對數日，未得其事。

translations.literal: Once he was put in prison, he was confronted for several days but the matter was not obtained.
translations.idiomatic: After he was imprisoned, days of interrogation failed to establish the capital charge.

sentences.zh: 夷簡持之益急，上聞，且貶焉，追舊從事以驗。

translations.literal: Yijian pressed the case ever more urgently; the emperor heard of it and demoted him, pursuing former staff to verify.
translations.idiomatic: Yijian pressed harder. The emperor heard the case and ordered demotion instead, summoning former staff to verify the lesser charges.

sentences.zh: 自貞元以來居方鎮者，為德宗所姑息，故窮極僭奢，無所畏忌。

translations.literal: Since Zhenyuan those who dwelt in regional commands were indulged and appeased by Dezong; therefore they exhausted presumption and luxury, without anything to fear.
translations.idiomatic: Since Zhenyuan, regional commanders indulged by Emperor Dezong had grown extravagantly presumptuous without fear of reprisal.

sentences.zh: 及憲宗即位，以法制臨下，夷簡首舉憑罪，故時議以為宜；

translations.literal: When Emperor Xianzong ascended, he faced subordinates with law and regulation; Yijian was first to raise Ping's crimes, so opinion of the time held this fitting.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xianzong ascended and governed by law, Yijian's prosecution of Ping was widely regarded as appropriate.

sentences.zh: 然繩之太過，物論又譏其深切矣。

translations.literal: Yet in binding him it was excessive; public discussion again criticized his severity.
translations.idiomatic: Yet public opinion also criticized Yijian for pressing the case too far.

sentences.zh: 鄭元鄭元，舉進士第，累遷御史中丞。

translations.literal: Zheng Yuan—Zheng Yuan passed the jinshi examination and was repeatedly transferred to Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Yuan passed the jinshi examination and rose to Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 貞元中為河中節度使杜確行軍司馬。

translations.literal: In Zhenyuan he was Campaigning Army Marshal for Du Que, Military Governor of Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhenyuan he served as campaigning marshal to Du Que, military governor of Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 確卒，遂繼為節度使，入拜尚書左丞。

translations.literal: When Que died he succeeded as Military Governor, entered and was appointed Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Que died he succeeded him as military governor and later entered court as Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 元和二年，轉戶部侍郎、兼御史大夫、判度支。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yuanhe he was transferred to Vice Minister of Revenue, concurrently Censor-in-Chief, and judged the Department of Public Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yuanhe (807) he became Vice Minister of Revenue, concurrent Censor-in-Chief, and head of the Department of Public Works.

sentences.zh: 三年春，遷刑部尚書，兼京兆尹。

translations.literal: In the spring of the third year he was transferred to Minister of Justice, concurrently Intendant of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the third year he was appointed Minister of Justice and concurrent Intendant of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 九月，復判度支，依前刑部尚書、兼御史大夫。

translations.literal: In the ninth month he again judged the Department of Public Works, continuing as before Minister of Justice and concurrently Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he resumed charge of the Department of Public Works while retaining his posts as Minister of Justice and Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 元性嚴毅，有威斷，更踐劇任，時稱其能。

translations.literal: Yuan's nature was stern and resolute, with awe-inspiring decisiveness; he again trod taxing duties, and his time praised his capability.
translations.idiomatic: Stern and decisive, Yuan took on demanding posts and was praised for his ability.

sentences.zh: 元和四年，以疾辭職，守本官，逾月卒。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yuanhe he resigned on account of illness, kept his original office, and died within a month.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Yuanhe he resigned on account of illness and died within a month.

sentences.zh: 杜兼杜兼，京兆人，貞觀中宰相杜正倫五代孫。

translations.literal: Du Jian—Du Jian was a native of Jingzhao, fifth-generation descendant of the Zhenguan Chancellor Du Zhenglun.
translations.idiomatic: Du Jian was a native of Jingzhao and fifth-generation descendant of Chancellor Du Zhenglun of the Zhenguan era.

sentences.zh: 舉進士，累辟諸府從事，拜濠州刺史。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination, was repeatedly summoned as staff to various prefectures, and was appointed Prefect of Haozhou.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination, served on several governors' staffs, and was appointed Prefect of Hao Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 兼性浮險，豪侈矜氣。

translations.literal: Jian's nature was floating and dangerous, extravagant and arrogant in spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Jian was unstable in character, extravagant, and arrogant.

sentences.zh: 屬貞元中德宗厭兵革，姑息戎鎮，至軍郡刺史，亦難於更代。

translations.literal: It happened that in Zhenyuan Dezong was weary of arms and armor and indulged military commands; even army prefecture prefects were difficult to replace.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenyuan, when Dezong was weary of war and indulged the commands, even prefects were hard to replace.

sentences.zh: 兼探上情，遂練卒修武，占召勁勇三千人以上聞，乃恣兇威。

translations.literal: Jian probed the emperor's disposition, then drilled soldiers and repaired arms, recruited and summoned more than three thousand stalwart brave men and reported upward, and then indulged violent authority.
translations.idiomatic: Reading the emperor's mood, Jian drilled troops, recruited more than three thousand strong men, reported this to court, and then ruled by brute force.

sentences.zh: 錄事參軍韋賞、團練判官陸楚，皆以守職論事忤兼，兼密誣奏二人通謀，扇動軍中。

translations.literal: Registrar Wei Shang and Training Commissioner Judge Lu Chu both, in holding their offices and discussing affairs, offended Jian; Jian secretly falsely memorialized that the two men conspired together and incited the army.
translations.idiomatic: Registrar Wei Shang and training commissioner Lu Chu offended Jian by doing their duty. Jian secretly memorialized that they were conspiring to stir up the army.

sentences.zh: 忽有制使至，兼率官吏迎於驛中，前呼韋賞、陸楚出，宣制杖殺之。

translations.literal: Suddenly an imperial envoy arrived; Jian led officials to welcome him at the post station, called forward Wei Shang and Lu Chu, proclaimed an edict, and had them beaten to death with staffs.
translations.idiomatic: When an imperial envoy suddenly arrived, Jian met him at the post station, had Wei Shang and Lu Chu brought out, and executed them by edict with the staff.

sentences.zh: 賞進士擢第，楚兗公象先之孫，皆名家，有士林之譽；

translations.literal: Shang had passed the jinshi examination; Chu was the grandson of Duke Xiangxian of Yan; all were eminent families with reputation among the forest of scholars.
translations.idiomatic: Shang had passed the jinshi examination; Chu was grandson of Duke Xiangxian of Yan. Both came from distinguished families with reputations among scholars.

sentences.zh: 一朝以無罪受戮，郡中股栗，天下冤嘆之。

translations.literal: In a single morning they were executed though guiltless; within the commandery thighs trembled, and all under Heaven lamented their injustice.
translations.idiomatic: Executed without guilt in a single morning, they left the command terrified and the empire mourning an injustice.

sentences.zh: 又誣奏李藩，將殺之，語在藩事中。

translations.literal: He again falsely memorialized against Li Fan and was about to kill him—the account is in Fan's biography.
translations.idiomatic: He also framed Li Fan and nearly had him killed; that story is told in Fan's biography.

sentences.zh: 故兼所至，人側目焉。

translations.literal: Therefore wherever Jian went, people looked askance.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever Jian went, people watched him with fear and distrust.

sentences.zh: 元和初，入為刑部、吏部郎中，拜給事中，除金商防禦使，旋授河南少尹、知府事，尋正拜河南尹。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanhe he entered as Director in the Ministries of Justice and Personnel, was appointed Attendant Gentleman, removed as Defense Commissioner of Jin-Shang, soon granted Vice Intendant of Henan with charge of prefectural affairs, and soon formally appointed Intendant of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yuanhe he entered court as Director in the Ministries of Justice and Personnel, became Attendant Gentleman, then Defense Commissioner of Jin-Shang, soon Vice Intendant of Henan, and finally full Intendant of Henan.

sentences.zh: 皆杜佑在相位所借護也。

translations.literal: All were owing to Du You's protection while in the chancellorship.
translations.idiomatic: All of this owed to the protection of Du You while he was chancellor.

sentences.zh: 元和四年，卒於官。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yuanhe he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office in the fourth year of Yuanhe (809).

sentences.zh: 裴玢裴玢，京兆人。

translations.literal: Pei Bin—Pei Bin was a native of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Bin was a native of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 五代祖疏勒國王綽，武德中來朝，授鷹揚大將軍，封天郡公，因留闕下，遂為京兆人。

translations.literal: His fifth-generation ancestor was Chuo, King of Kucha; in Wude he came to court, was appointed General of the Soaring Hawk, enfeoffed as Duke of Tian Commandery, and because he remained at the capital became a native of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: His fifth-generation ancestor Chuo, king of Kucha, came to court in the Wude era, was appointed General of the Soaring Hawk and enfeoffed as Duke of Tian Commandery, and remained at the capital, where the family became Jingzhao natives.

sentences.zh: 玢初事金吾將軍論惟明為傔力。

translations.literal: Bin at first served the Golden Crow General Lun Weiming as a personal attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Bin first served as personal attendant to Golden Crow General Lun Weiming.

sentences.zh: 德宗幸奉天，以戰功封忠義郡王。

translations.literal: When Dezong visited Fengtian, for battle achievements he was enfeoffed as Prince of Zhongyi Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Dezong went to Fengtian, Bin was enfeoffed as Prince of Zhongyi Commandery for his service in battle.

sentences.zh: 惟明鎮鄜坊，累署玢為都虞候。

translations.literal: Weiming commanded Mei-Fang and repeatedly appointed Bin Chief Army Inspector.
translations.idiomatic: When Weiming governed Mei and Fang, he repeatedly appointed Bin chief army inspector.

sentences.zh: 後節度王棲曜卒，中軍將何朝宗謀作亂，中夜縱火，玢匿身不救火，遲明而擒朝宗。

translations.literal: Later when Military Governor Wang Qiyao died, the Central Army General He Chaozong plotted rebellion, set fire at midnight; Bin hid himself and did not fight the fire, and at dawn captured Chaozong.
translations.idiomatic: After Military Governor Wang Qiyao died, Central Army General He Chaozong plotted a coup and set fires at midnight. Bin held back from fighting the blaze, then at dawn seized Chaozong.

sentences.zh: 德宗發三司使按問，竟斬朝宗及行軍司馬崔輅，以同州刺史劉公濟為節度使，以玢為坊州長史、兼侍御史，充行軍司馬。

translations.literal: Dezong dispatched the Three Offices envoy to investigate; in the end Chaozong and the Campaigning Army Marshal Cui Lu were beheaded; Liu Gongji, Prefect of Tongzhou, was made Military Governor, and Bin was made Chief Administrator of Fangzhou, concurrently Attendant Censor, filling the post of Campaigning Army Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong sent the Three Offices to investigate. Chaozong and campaigning marshal Cui Lu were executed. Liu Gongji of Tong Prefecture became military governor, and Bin was appointed Chief Administrator of Fang Prefecture, concurrent Attendant Censor, and campaigning marshal.

sentences.zh: 明年，公濟卒，拜玢鄜州刺史、兼御史大夫，充節度觀察等使。

translations.literal: The next year Gongji died; Bin was appointed Prefect of Meizhou, concurrently Censor-in-Chief, and filled the posts of Military Governor, Observer, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, when Gongji died, Bin was appointed Prefect of Mei Prefecture, Censor-in-Chief, and full military governor.

sentences.zh: 三年，改授山南西道節度觀察等使。

translations.literal: In the third year he was changed and appointed Military Governor and Observer of Shannan West Circuit and the like.
translations.idiomatic: Three years later he was transferred to military governor of Shannan West Circuit.

sentences.zh: 玢歷二鎮，頗以公清苦節為政；

translations.literal: Bin passed through two commands and rather governed with public integrity, austerity, and moral discipline.
translations.idiomatic: Over two commands Bin governed with public integrity, austerity, and moral discipline.

sentences.zh: 不交權幸，不務貢獻，蔬食敝衣，居處才避風雨，而廩庫饒實，三軍百姓安業，近代將帥無比焉。

translations.literal: He did not associate with the powerful and favored, did not pursue tribute offerings, ate vegetables and wore worn clothes, his dwelling barely sheltering from wind and rain, yet granaries were full and solid, the Three Armies and common people were secure in their occupations—among recent generals and commanders there was none comparable.
translations.idiomatic: He shunned the powerful, refused extravagant tribute, ate plainly and dressed poorly, and lived in quarters that barely kept out the weather. Yet his granaries were full, troops and civilians secure in their livelihoods—a record unmatched among recent commanders.

sentences.zh: 及綿疾辭位，請歸長安。

translations.literal: When his chronic illness led him to resign his post, he requested to return to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: When chronic illness forced him to resign, he asked to return to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 元和七年卒，年六十五，贈尚書左僕射，諡曰節。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Yuanhe he died, age sixty-five; he was posthumously enfeoffed as Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, posthumous title Jie.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the seventh year of Yuanhe (812) at the age of sixty-five. The court posthumously appointed him Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs with the posthumous title Jie (Integrity).

sentences.zh: 薛伾薛伾，勝州刺史渙之子。

translations.literal: Xue Pi—Xue Pi was the son of Huan, Prefect of Shengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Pi was the son of Huan, Prefect of Sheng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 尚父汾陽王召置麾下，著名於諸將間。

translations.literal: The Sagely Father Prince of Fenyang summoned and placed him under his banner; he was famed among the various generals.
translations.idiomatic: The Sagely Father, Prince of Fenyang, took him into his service, and he won renown among the generals.

sentences.zh: 左僕射李揆使西蕃，伾為將從役。

translations.literal: Left Vice Director Li Kui was envoy to the Western Tibetans; Pi served as general in attendance on the mission.
translations.idiomatic: When Left Vice Director Li Kui went as envoy to Tibet, Pi served on his military escort.

sentences.zh: 時賊泚之難，昆夷赴義，伾馳騎鄉導，至於武功，擢授左威衛將軍。

translations.literal: At the time of the disaster of the rebel Zhu Ci, the Kunyi came in righteousness; Pi galloped as guide through the countryside as far as Wugong, and was promoted and appointed General of the Left Majestic Guard.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhu Ci's rebellion, when allied forces came to the emperor's aid, Pi rode ahead as guide as far as Wugong and was promoted to General of the Left Majestic Guard.

sentences.zh: 使絕域者前後數四，累遷左金吾衛大將軍、檢校工部尚書、兼將作監，出為鄜坊觀察使。

translations.literal: As envoy to distant regions four times in succession before and after, he was repeatedly transferred to Left General of the Golden Crow Guard, Acting Minister of Works, concurrently Director of the Directorate of Works, and went out as Military Governor of Mei-Fang.
translations.idiomatic: He served four times as envoy to distant regions and rose through Left General of the Golden Crow Guard, Acting Minister of Works, concurrent Director of the Directorate of Works, to military governor of Mei and Fang.

sentences.zh: 元和八年，卒於官，贈潞州大都督。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Yuanhe he died in office and was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Governor of Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office in the eighth year of Yuanhe (813) and was posthumously appointed Grand Governor of Lu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰史臣曰：薛播溫敏有文，鮑防董戎無術，李、嚴太原之政，可謂美矣。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: Xue Bo was gentle, quick, and possessed of letters; Bao Fang supervised troops without method; the governments of Li and Yan at Taiyuan may be called beautiful.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer remarks: Xue Bo was gracious, quick-witted, and literate; Bao Fang was no soldier; and the Taiyuan administrations of Li Ziliang and Yan Shou were genuinely admirable.

sentences.zh: 蕭昕抱則哲之知，杜亞懷非次之望。

translations.literal: Xiao Xin embraced the knowledge of one who follows the wise; Du Ya harbored expectations beyond his proper rank.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Xin possessed the discernment of a sage; Du Ya entertained ambitions beyond his station.

sentences.zh: 王緯清潔而傷苛碎，若初善理而性剛嚴。

translations.literal: Wang Wei was clean and pure yet harmed by harsh minuteness; Ruochu was good at administration yet stern and strict in nature.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wei was scrupulously honest but excessively meticulous; Ruochu was capable in administration but stern by nature.

sentences.zh: 于頎好任機權，趨附勢利。

translations.literal: Yu Yi loved to employ stratagems and power, and rushed to attach himself to profit and influence.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yi loved intrigue and courted the powerful.

sentences.zh: 盧徵厚斂貨賄，結托中人。

translations.literal: Lu Zheng heavily collected goods and bribes and formed bonds with palace eunuchs.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zheng extorted wealth and cultivated palace eunuchs.

sentences.zh: 楊憑好奢，鄭元有斷。

translations.literal: Yang Ping loved extravagance; Zheng Yuan had decisiveness.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Ping loved luxury; Zheng Yuan had decisive authority.

sentences.zh: 杜兼殺戮端士，怙亂邀君。

translations.literal: Du Jian slaughtered upright gentlemen and relied on disorder to importune the ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Du Jian killed upright officials and used disorder to impose on the throne.

sentences.zh: 裴玢發奸謀，安民和眾。

translations.literal: Pei Bin exposed treacherous plots and settled the people and harmonized the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Bin exposed conspiracies and brought peace to troops and people alike.

sentences.zh: 而玢敝衣糲食，不交權幸，帑庾咸實，郡邑以寧。

translations.literal: Yet Bin wore worn clothes and ate coarse food, did not associate with the powerful and favored, treasuries were all full, and commanderies and districts were thereby tranquil.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he dressed plainly, shunned the powerful, filled the treasuries, and kept his jurisdictions at peace.

sentences.zh: 若夫君子無求備於人，舍短從長，彰善癉惡，則裴玢之善，抑之更揚；

translations.literal: As for the gentleman who does not demand completeness in others, abandons the short and follows the long, displays good and exposes evil—then Pei Bin's goodness, though suppressed, is further raised aloft.
translations.idiomatic: If a gentleman does not demand perfection in others, overlooks faults for strengths, and makes virtue plain while exposing evil, then Pei Bin's goodness, though understated, shines all the brighter.

sentences.zh: 杜兼之惡，欲蓋而彰耳。

translations.literal: Du Jian's evil—one wishes to cover it yet it is displayed all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Du Jian's wickedness, the more one would hide it, the more plainly it shows.
